x: Facts on current events as of 8 October 2026. A code in square brackets, for example [NBC599] , names the source of a statement. The codes are explained in Reference F . "GK" means general knowledge that I did not open in a source during this work. The list of all files is in the README .

t: 1. The question this file answers
p: Philippine PFM Atlas: the big picture
x: How do the parts of Philippine public financial management (PFM) relate to each other: the functions, the authorities that perform them, the information systems that these authorities use, and the records that pass from one to the next? This file gives the whole on a few pages. Each part has its own chapter with the steps, the documents, the systems and the sources.

t: 2. The whole in plain words
p: Philippine PFM Atlas: the big picture
x: Public money does not belong to the person who handles it. For this reason a rule decides, at every step, who may do what. PFM has five parts. Only the first part is a sequence of steps. Diagram 00a shows the five parts. Part What happens Order in time Chapters A. Decide Plan, set the fiscal frame, prepare the budget, pass the budget law One after the other, for one fiscal year 01 to 04 B. Execute Three lines of steps: legal authority, the claim, cash At the same time. Money may leave the Treasury only where the three meet 05 to 07 , 10 to 12 , 15 C. Record and check Registries, books of accounts, property records, certifications by officers At the same time as every act of part B 07 , 08 , 13 D. Close each period Reconcile, report, audit, oversee At the end of each month, quarter and year. The audit of single payments continues during the whole year 08 , 09 , 18 E. What remains Assets, debts, and promises that bind later budgets After the year 11 , 13 , 19 The rest of this section explains part B together with part C, because a drawing with one line of steps cannot show them. In part B the rules control three different things. A fourth line of work, part C, records all three. No. Line The question The main steps Who is responsible 1 Legal authority May the government spend for this purpose in this year? Appropriation, then allotment, then obligation Congress, DBM, the budget unit of the agency 2 The claim Why does the government owe this amount to this party? For a purchase: plan, procurement, contract, delivery, acceptance. For a salary: position, appointment, service rendered. Other payments have other steps (section 12) The agency, its Bids and Awards Committee, the supplier or the employee 3 Cash Is there money to pay on the day? Collection and borrowing, the single account of the Treasury, cash authority, payment, replenishment BIR, BOC, the banks, BTr, BSP, DBM 4 Records and control Is each act recorded when it happens, and is each fact stated by an officer who is responsible for it? Registries, journal entries, certifications on each document, reports, audit The budget, accounting, cash and property units of the agency, BTr, COA Lines 1, 3 and 4 have the same steps for every payment. Line 2 has a different form for each kind of payment. A purchase is one form of claim, and the following paragraphs use it as the example. The lines run at the same time. They do not form one line. A payment can be made only at a point where the lines meet. Two lines meet where one act needs a result from both of them. For one payment under a contract there are three such points ( diagram 00d ). An allotment meets an award . Only then may the agency sign the contract and record the obligation. The procurement law says that no contract may be awarded before the funding is approved and effective [RA12009 s.12] . The Auditing Code says that no contract may be entered into before the accounting official has certified that funds are available [PD1445 s.86] . An obligation meets an accepted delivery . Only then is the amount a payable. The Manual defines accounts payable as obligations for which goods, services or projects "have been delivered/rendered/completed and accepted" [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.2] . The budget reports call such an amount due and demandable [JC2019-1] . A claim in order meets a cash authority that has enough balance. Only then may the head of accounting certify "Cash available" on the voucher, and only then may the head of the agency approve the payment [GAM-V2 App.32] [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] . No check and no payment order may be issued without a covering Notice of Cash Allocation [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.3] . The second point has a lawful exception, the advance payment. The Auditing Code allows no advance payment "Except with the prior approval of the President" [PD1445 s.88] . An order of the President of 2011 gave this approval for goods under the earlier procurement law [MO15-2011] . The procurement rules of 2025 name the cases: for example an advance of not more than 15 percent of a works contract, on the written request of the contractor and against an irrevocable standby letter of credit, a bank guarantee or a surety bond [IRR12009 s.71.2.5] . In such a case the security replaces the accepted delivery. Chapter 07, section 7.2 , follows such a contract with amounts. A case where the whole works: an agency starts the bidding before the year begins, which the law allows. The budget law takes effect in January, and for an item without conditions the law itself is the allotment. The agency awards and signs in February, and the budget unit enters the obligation in its registry. The supplier delivers in May, the agency accepts, and the accounting unit records a payable. The Notice of Cash Allocation of the second quarter has enough balance, so the voucher is certified and approved. The agency sends the payment order, the bank credits the supplier, and the Treasury repays the bank [RA12009 s.12] [NBC599] [CL2013-16A] [GAM-V1 Annex H] . A case where it fails: the delivery is accepted on 28 June, and the voucher reaches the head of accounting on 2 July. The unused part of the cash authority of the second quarter lapsed on the last working day of June [NBC599 s.4.2.1.6] . If the cash authority of the third quarter is needed for other payments, the head of accounting cannot certify that cash is available, and the voucher waits [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] . The agency holds a valid obligation and a payable, and it cannot pay. Nothing is wrong in any single line of steps. The lines did not meet in time. A drawing with one line of steps cannot show this. I think this is the main reason why a map of "the PFM process" as one flow looks incomplete, even when it has many boxes. Five more facts increase the difficulty. Three budgets are active in one calendar year. In 2026, agencies close the accounts of fiscal year 2025, execute the budget of 2026 and prepare the budget of 2027 ( diagram 00e ). The records do not wait for the payment. The allotment and the obligation are entered in registries when they occur, and they have no journal entry. The first journal entry is made when the cash authority arrives. The payable is recorded when the delivery is accepted [GAM-V1 Annex H] . Section 7 and chapter 08 show which unit writes which record, and when. Not all money follows the route of a purchase. Salaries, the share of local governments, support to government corporations, transfers to other bodies, cash aid to persons, interest on debt and direct payments by lenders each have another form of claim (section 12). One spending has several amounts. The authority, the commitment, the accepted delivery, the cash paid and the result are recorded on different dates and appear in different reports. For the same program and the same year these amounts differ, and none of them is wrong (section 9, and chapter 08, section 12 ). Some decisions of today bind the budgets of later years. A contract for several years, a partnership with a private firm and a guarantee are such decisions. The appropriation of the present year does not show them in full ( chapter 19 ). Terms used in this file, in the words of the law where I could read them. An appropriation is "an authorization made by law or other legislative enactment, directing payment out of government funds under specified conditions or for specified purposes". An allotment is "an authorization issued by the Department of the Budget to an agency, which allows it to incur obligations for specified amounts contained in a legislative appropriation". An obligation is "an amount committed to be paid by the Government for any lawful act made by an authorized officer for and in behalf of the government" [EO292-B6 s.2] . A Notice of Cash Allocation (NCA) "specifies the maximum amount of withdrawal that an entity can make from a government bank for the period indicated" [GAM-V1 Ch.5 s.38] . A voucher is the document that approves one claim for payment. A registry is a running list with balances that the budget unit keeps. The books of accounts are the journals and ledgers that the accounting unit keeps by double entry. The glossary is in Reference E .

The results of year N (actual figures, audit findings, evaluations) return to the plans and budgets of later years, because the budget of year N+1 is already prepared and voted while year N is executed. A case where the order of part A matters: Congress may not increase the appropriations that the President recommended, so an amount that is missing in the proposal of step 3 cannot be added in step 4 beyond that limit [EO292-B6 s.24] . A case where no order exists: the accounting unit does not wait for the payment to record a delivery. It records the payable when the delivery is accepted, and the budget unit recorded the obligation months before [GAM-V1 Annex H] .

t: Diagram 00a  The whole of PFM for the national government: what happens in order, what happens at the same time, and the chapter for each part
p: Philippine PFM Atlas: the big picture
x: Code file: diagrams/mermaid/00a_pfm_cycle_overview.mmd . Rendered image: rendered/00a_pfm_cycle_overview.png . Question: which parts form public financial management (PFM) in the Philippines, which of them follow one another, which of them happen at the same time, and which chapter of this atlas describes each one? Idea: only the decisions of part A follow one another for one fiscal year. In part B three lines of steps run at the same time, and money may leave the Treasury only where all three have a result for the same amount ( diagram 00d ). Part C is not a later step: every act of part B writes a record at the time of the act. Part D happens at the end of each month, quarter and year. Part E is what stays after the year. How to read it: a solid arrow between two frames = the lower frame needs the result of the upper frame. The dotted arrow from B to C = every act in B writes a record in C at the same time. Inside a frame, an arrow = the order of the steps of that line. The frames at the sides are active during the whole year. The cycle is not a simple loop: results return to the plans and budgets of LATER fiscal years, so the last node is drawn as an exit and not as an arrow back to part A. Why the records stand at every act: the Manual records the allotment and the obligation in registries when they occur, makes the first journal entry when the Notice of Cash Allocation arrives, and records the payable when the delivery is accepted, before any payment [GAM-V1 Annex H] . Recording is therefore not a step after payment. Sources: DBM primer on the budget process [PRIMER] , FY 2027 Budget Call [NBM156] , FY 2026 release guidelines [NBC599] , procurement law [RA12009] , reporting circular [JC2019-1] , the Government Accounting Manual for the records of each unit and the order of the entries [GAM-V1 Ch.2 s.8, s.12, Ch.3, Annex H] , Auditing Code [PD1445 s.41] , PFM Reforms Roadmap 2024-2028 [ROADMAP2024] . The arrangement in five parts is my own. Limit: local governments and government corporations have their own complete cycles ( chapters 14 and 15). Here they appear only where national money passes to them.

t: 5.1 Kinds of arrows, and what would show that an arrow is wrong
p: Philippine PFM Atlas: the big picture
x: An arrow in a diagram is a statement about the process. The statements are of different kinds, and each kind is tested in a different way. This atlas uses nine kinds. Where one diagram draws more than one kind, the comment lines at its start explain how each kind is drawn. Kind of arrow What it states Example Where the atlas uses it An observation that would show it to be wrong Order of acts Act B may happen only after act A, or only when state A exists The contract may be signed only when an allotment and an award both exist 00d, the lane diagrams, the state diagrams A rule or a lawful case in which B happens without A. First example: the bidding does not need an allotment. Only the award needs it, so an arrow from "allotment" to "invitation to bid" would be wrong. Second example: an advance payment is lawful without an accepted delivery, so diagram 00d draws it as a separate path Writing of a record An act produces an entry in a registry or in a book at the time of the act The acceptance of a delivery produces the journal entry for the payable 00d (dotted arrow to a grey node), 08e The entry is made at another time, by another unit, or not at all. Example: an obligation is entered in a registry and has no journal entry, so an arrow from "obligation" to "journal" would be wrong Authority A gives B the right or the duty to act DBM gives an agency an allotment 00g (thin solid arrow), the sequence diagrams The legal text gives the right in another way. Example: for an item without conditions the budget law itself is the allotment, so an arrow "DBM issues a SARO" is wrong for that item Document A document passes from A to B The agency sends the payment order to the bank The sequence diagrams The document goes to another receiver, or it does not exist as a separate document Money An amount leaves one account and enters another The Treasury repays the servicing bank 00g (thick arrow), 07d, 11a, 16g (green arrow) No account is debited. Example: a Notice of Cash Allocation is a limit, and an arrow "DBM sends cash to the agency" is wrong Information B receives data about an event. Nothing is authorized and no money moves Agencies report to DBM, COA and BTr 00g (dotted arrow), 08b The report goes to another body, or B does not receive it Link between systems Data pass from system A to system B ADRS delivers a release document to an agency 16b, 16g, and the register in Reference B, section 4 A person enters the same data a second time, or the data pass as a file or on paper. The register gives the evidence for each flow Reference between records Record B contains the number of record A The payment order contains the number of the obligation request 17b, 17c The form has no such field, or the field is free text Classification A record belongs to a class An obligation has an object code of UACS 17a, 17d The record has no code, or two systems use different lists of codes A case where the kinds matter: a drawing shows an arrow from DBM to an agency with the label "NCA". Read as money, it says that DBM pays the agency. Read as authority, it says that DBM sets a limit up to which the bank may pay. Only the second reading is correct [NBC599] . A case where the kinds are not enough: an arrow of the kind "order of acts" is correct by the rule, and practice differs. The atlas draws the rules. Where an assessment reports that practice differs, the chapter says so in its section on weaknesses. An arrow of the kind "order of acts" between two parts of diagram 00a does not say that the lower part starts when the upper part has ended. Parts B and C happen at the same time, and the diagram draws them side by side for this reason.

t: 6. Three lines of steps, three meeting points, and the records
p: Philippine PFM Atlas: the big picture
x: Diagram 00d is the formal version of section 2. It uses the form of a Petri net. A rounded node is a state that is true or not yet true. A rectangle is an act by the persons named in it. An act with two incoming solid arrows needs both states to be true. The colours mark the lines: blue for legal authority, green for the claim, orange for cash, grey for records and audit. The three meeting points are the acts t3 (sign the contract and obligate), t6 (prepare and examine the claim) and t6c (certify cash and approve the voucher). The grey nodes r1 to r7 are records. A dotted arrow from an act to a grey node means that the act writes this record at the time of the act. The table lists them. No record waits for the payment. Record Written at the act By which unit Content Basis r1 Release of the allotment Budget unit Allotment in the registries. No journal entry GAM-V1 Ch.3 ss.8-10, Annex H r2 Contract signed, obligation request approved Budget unit Obligation in the registry. No journal entry GAM-V1 Ch.3 s.15, Annex H r3 NCA issued by DBM Accounting unit First journal entry: debit Cash-Modified Disbursement System (MDS), Regular, credit Subsidy from National Government. The NCA is entered in the registry of the NCA GAM-V1 Ch.5 s.38, Ch.6 s.3 r4 Delivery inspected and accepted Property unit, accounting unit, budget unit Acceptance report. Journal entry: debit the asset or expense, credit Accounts Payable. The payable is entered in part C of the obligation request GAM-V1 Ch.8 s.15, Annex H. GAM-V2 App.11 r5 Voucher certified and approved Accounting unit Voucher with its number. The amount is entered as used in the registry of the NCA GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12 r6 Payment order or check issued Cash unit, accounting unit, budget unit Daily report of payment orders or checks issued. Journal entry: debit Accounts Payable, credit Cash-MDS, Regular and Due to BIR. Payment entered in the registries. One copy goes to the COA auditor with the paid vouchers GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.56, s.57 r7 Treasury repays the bank BTr Books of the Treasury: debit Subsidy to NGAs, credit Cash in Bank GAM-V1 Annex H The diagram has a small separate chain at its side: end of a period, closing, reports, audit of the statements. It is separate because the closing of a period does not follow one payment. It follows the calendar, and it uses all records that exist on that day. The dashed green path is the lawful exception of section 2: for an advance payment, a security posted by the contractor replaces the accepted delivery. The form has three limits, and all matter if the diagram is used as a model. An allotment and a cash authority are balances, not single items. A model needs an amount on each of them. One line of the budget funds many contracts, and one contract has many payments. One case identifier therefore does not fit all places of the net. Chapter 17 explains this with an example. The green line is drawn for a purchase. For a salary, a transfer, debt service or a refund, another event creates the claim. Diagram 07h compares the forms. A difference inside the Manual: its worked example records the payable at delivery, from the delivery receipt and the acceptance report [GAM-V1 Annex H] . Its section on payment orders says that payables are recorded "based on approved DVs" [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.57] . The diagram follows the worked example. Under the second reading, record r4 would be written at act t6c.

t: Diagram 00d  Three lines of steps, the three points where they must meet, and the record that each act writes (one payment under a contract)
p: Philippine PFM Atlas: the big picture
x: Code file: diagrams/mermaid/00d_four_chains.mmd . Rendered image: rendered/00d_four_chains.png . Question: which conditions must all be true before one payment to a contractor can be made, who makes each condition true, and which record is written at each act? Idea: a payment is not the end of one line of steps. Three lines of steps run at the same time: legal authority, the claim, and cash. A payment is possible only when they meet. The fourth line, the records, does not come after the payment: each act writes its record when it happens. A diagram with one line of steps hides both facts. Form (Petri-net style): rounded node p = a state that can be true or not yet true. Rectangle t = an act by the persons named in it. An act with two incoming solid arrows needs BOTH states. A grey node r = a record. A dotted arrow from an act to a grey node = the act writes this record at the time of the act. Colours: blue = legal authority to spend. Green = the claim: the contract, the work and its acceptance. Orange = cash. Grey = records, reports and audit. The small separate chain (pT to p19): the closing of a period does not follow one payment. It follows the calendar, and it uses all records that exist on that day. The audit of one paid transaction (t14) follows the payment, because the paid voucher goes to the auditor with the daily report of payment orders issued [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.56] . The three meeting points: t3 (allotment meets award), t6 (obligation meets accepted delivery), t6c (the claim meets cash authority). The third point is the certificate "cash available" on the voucher: the head of accounting looks into the registry of the NCA, and when the balance is not sufficient the voucher is kept until cash is available [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] . No check and no payment order may be issued without a covering NCA [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.3] . THE EXCEPTION AT t6: the law allows no advance payment without the prior approval of the President, and no payment without a certificate that the delivery was inspected and accepted [PD1445 s.88] . The procurement rules give that approval in defined cases: for works, an advance of not more than 15 percent on the written request of the contractor and against an irrevocable standby letter of credit, a bank guarantee or a surety bond [IRR12009 s.71.2.5] . In that case the security (p8b) replaces the accepted delivery (p8). The dashed green path shows it. Diagram 07i follows such a contract with amounts. The dotted arrow into t9 is a read arc: DBM consults the cash position of the Treasury but does not consume it when it issues an NCA. Limits of this form: (1) allotment and NCA are balances, so each token would need an amount. (2) One appropriation line funds many contracts and one contract has many payments, so one case identifier does not fit all places (see 17d). (3) The claim is drawn for a purchase. For a salary, a transfer, debt service or a refund another event creates the claim ( diagram 07h ). Sources: allotment before commitment and NCA before payment [NBC599] . Question: for one fiscal year, which authority acts at each step from plan to audit, where do two lines of work run at the same time and then have to meet, and at which step is each record written? Idea: the steps of deciding (plan, fiscal frame, proposal, law) follow one another. In execution, two lines of work run at the same time three times, and each time both must be finished before the next step. The records are not a last step: the text of each step names the record that is written at that step. Only the closing of a period and the audit of the statements follow the calendar. t: Diagram 00h  One contract with dates: a school building paid from the FY 2026 budget (invented example, real rules)
p: Philippine PFM Atlas: the big picture
x: Code file: diagrams/mermaid/00h_worked_example_one_contract.mmd . Rendered image: rendered/00h_worked_example_one_contract.png . Question: the other diagrams show the order of steps. How long does each step take for one contract, in which fiscal year does each step occur, and on which date is each record written? Idea: one contract extends over three calendar years. Its budget is prepared in the year before, the work is done in the budget year, and the last progress payment, the release of the retention money and the audit occur in the year after. The four sections are the four lines of steps of diagram 00d : authority, the claim, cash, records. The records are written on the dates of the acts, and not after the last payment. THE EXAMPLE IS INVENTED. The agency, the amounts and the dates of the single steps are not real. The rules that fix the earliest and latest dates are real, and they are listed here with their sources. The example: an agency builds a school building for PHP 48 million. The amount is a capital outlay in the FY 2026 budget law, without a pre-condition for release. The contractor asks for an advance of 15 percent. The work takes nine months and is billed in three parts. Rules used, with sources: the agency may hold the bidding before the budget law exists, once the President's budget is submitted, but it may not award before the funding is in effect and the head of the agency has approved the final procurement plan [IRR12009 s.12] [RA12009 s.12] . The FY 2026 budget law took effect on 5 January 2026, and the law itself is the allotment for items without pre-conditions [NBC599] . Award within 60 days from the opening of bids, contract within 10 days after the notice of award [IRR12009 s.66, s.67] , notice to proceed within 3 days [RA12009 s.66] . The chief accountant certifies that funds are available before the contract [PD1445 s.86] . Advance to a works contractor: not more than 15 percent, on written request and against a letter of credit, bank guarantee or surety bond [IRR12009 s.71.2.5] . Progress billing not more often than once a month. Each bill is reduced by the part of the advance that is recovered and by the retention money [IRR12009 s.71.2.7, s.71.2.8] . Defects liability period of one year from completion to final acceptance. The retention money is due for release upon final acceptance [IRR12009 s.90.2.2, s.71.2.8] . A regular NCA lapses at the end of its quarter, and the regular NCA of a later period also covers payables of earlier years [NBC599 s.4.2] . The bank credits the payee within two banking days after it receives the payment order [CL2018-14] . Quarterly reports within 30 days after each quarter, and the report on unpaid obligations within 30 days after the year [JC2019-1] . Year-end statements to COA by 14 February, annual report of COA by 30 September [PD1445 s.41] . Capital outlays of FY 2026 may be obligated until 31 December 2027 (the table in my copy was partly unreadable) [NBC599 s.3.3] . Records, with sources: the obligation is entered in the registry and has no journal entry. An advance is recorded as Advances to Contractors. Each certified progress billing is recorded as Construction in Progress and as Accounts Payable. At the turn-over of the completed building the cost moves to the account Buildings. Retention money is held as Guaranty/Security Deposits Payable until it is released [GAM-V1 Ch.3 s.15, Ch.10 s.8, Annex H] . Where the example fails on purpose: the third bill is certified on 20 November 2026, but the cash authority of the fourth quarter is fully used. The contractor is paid on 15 February 2027. During these weeks the amount is a cost of construction and a payable in the books, an obligation in the registry, and no disbursement. Diagram 08c explains these measures. General knowledge, not opened in a source here: the dates of the budget preparation in 2025 (the pattern of 2026 is used), and the month in which the audit report of the agency is issued.

t: 10. The information systems
p: Philippine PFM Atlas: the big picture
x: Each institution built systems for its own part of the process. Diagram 00c shows them by owner. The table names the main system at each stage. The full inventory, with owner, user and recipient of each system, is in Reference B . The flows of data and documents between the systems and the offices are in chapter 16 . Reference B, section 4 , lists every flow with six properties: what passes, the kind of flow, the carrier, the stage of use, the check that compares both sides, and the basis. Stage System and owner Basis Investment program PIPOL (DEPDev) PIP-MEMO Budget proposals OSBPS (DBM) NBM156 Positions GMIS (DBM) GMIS Release documents ADRS (DBM), with a public record for verification ADRS , DBM-BLOCKCHAIN Execution plans and reports URS (DBM) NBC599 , JC2019-1 Procurement PhilGEPS (PS-DBM), with a Virtual Store and an eMarketplace for common-use items. The earlier version of the portal takes no new posting from 1 March 2026 RA12009 s.20, PS-FAQ , GPPB2025-09 Obligations and books in most agencies Registries and accounting software of the agency, or the eBudget and eNGAS of COA COA-GAS Obligations, payments, receipts, property and books in agencies of the rollout BTMS (DBM) CL2025-8 Payment Facility of the servicing bank, for example the eMDS of LBP eMDS Financial statements to COA AFR System (COA) COA-GAS Tax returns and payments eFPS, eBIRForms, payment gateways (BIR). The E2M customs system (BOC), and Payment Application Secure for customs collections BIR-PAY , BOC-MOD , PAS Collections, cash, securities, assets NGCDS, eTRAMS, NRoSS, National Asset Registry System (BTr) BTR-SYS Local fiscal reports eSRE (BLGF) eSRE Publication for the public COMPASS portal (DBM), in use since 26 June 2026 COMPASS-LAUNCH , EO126 Four statements summarize the present state and the plan. Today the systems are separate. Data passes between them by reports, by files and by typing the same data again. The Roadmap names three gaps: the same report is prepared more than once, processing is manual, and the systems are not integrated [ROADMAP2024] . Many flows between an agency, its bank, the Treasury and the auditor are numbered copies of paper forms. The Manual of 2015 prescribes them copy by copy [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.56] . The plan is a core with interfaces, not one system for everything. Executive Order No. 29 of 2023 directs all national government entities to adopt the Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS). The Roadmap makes BTMS its core and connects the other systems to it through interfaces. Agencies keep their systems [EO29] [ROADMAP2024] [SFA6] . The procurement rules of 2025 also name the IFMIS: the electronic payment system for procurement "shall be defined in the context of the Integrated Financial Management Information System to be developed by the DBM, COA, and Department of Finance" [IRR12009 s.21] . The core is at an early stage, and official statements on its state differ. A press report of DBM statements and the action plan of the Roadmap say: DBM and BTr use BTMS, five more pilot agencies prepare in 2026, and the plan is about 110 to 115 agencies in 2027 and 198 in 2028, 315 in total [INQ-BTMS] [SFA6] . A speech of the DBM Secretary of 22 January 2026 says that BTMS was launched in 2024, was piloted with seven agencies in 2025, and reaches 155 agencies in 2026 [DBM-SPEECH26] . The atlas uses the first account, because two sources agree on it and it is the more detailed one. Reference G lists the difference. A portal for the public exists since June 2026. DBM launched the COMPASS portal on 26 June 2026. Executive Order No. 126 of 28 September 2026 makes it the platform of the government for budget and expenditure disclosures, and requires national agencies and government corporations to submit and update their information. Each agency is responsible for the accuracy of what it submits. The order permits the use of distributed ledger technology and does not require it [COMPASS-LAUNCH] [EO126] . I read the order in press releases, not in its text. Chapter 16, section 11 , gives the details.

t: 11. Codes and numbers that connect the records
p: Philippine PFM Atlas: the big picture
x: Two kinds of mark connect the records of the process, and each has a different function. A classification code says to which group an amount belongs. The Unified Accounts Code Structure (UACS) is the common classification of the budget, the books and the reports: 54 digits in five segments, for funding source, organization, location, program and object [JC2017-1] . The Auditing Code requires such a classification: "A common terminology and classification shall be used consistently throughout the budget, the accounts and the financial reports" [PD1445 s.115] . The last segment is the same code in the budget and in the books by its construction: the object code of UACS is the account code of the Revised Chart of Accounts followed by two more digits [GAM-V3 Ch.2] . A document number says which single record this is. The forms of the Manual carry the numbers of the records before them. The purchase order carries the number of the obligation request. The acceptance report carries the number of the purchase order. The voucher carries the number of the obligation request. Each line of the payment order carries the number of the obligation request [GAM-V2 App.61, App.62, App.32, App.42] . In this way one transaction can be followed. The totals of two systems can be compared only when both use the same classification, or when a documented table translates the codes of one into the codes of the other. UACS is the common classification that COA, DBM and DOF prescribed [JC2017-1] . The sources that I read name no translation table between PFM systems, and the action plan of the Roadmap reports that classification codes are not consistent across systems [SFA6] . UACS is not sufficient to follow one transaction, because two contracts under one budget line have the same code on every record. Chapter 17 shows the chain of numbers for one purchase, form by form, and the places where a form has no field for the number of the record before it. One link at the start of a purchase has neither a code nor a number. The form of the procurement plan that is mandatory since 21 September 2025 names the source of funds of each line in words, for example "GAA 2026 - Current Appropriation", and has no column for a budget code [APP-FORM2025] . The form of 2015 began with a column "Code (PAP)", and its circular does not say which code belongs there [APP-FORM] . A line of the plan can now be matched with a line of the budget law only by words and amounts. In a purchase, the first record that carries the program code and the object code is the obligation request.

t: 15. How far this atlas can be relied on
p: Philippine PFM Atlas: the big picture
x: Every table of steps has a column "Basis", and every diagram file contains comment lines that name its sources. Three marks are used. Mark Meaning A code, for example [NBC599] I opened this source during this work and found the fact in it GK General knowledge. I did not open a source for it. Check these lines first Inference My own conclusion from two or more sources The sources were read in two ways. A statement from a source of the first kind is more certain than a statement from a source of the second kind. Read as files, word for word: the three volumes of the Government Accounting Manual of 2015 [GAM-V1] [GAM-V2] [GAM-V3] , the Government Auditing Code [PD1445] , and the Implementing Rules of the procurement law as approved in February 2025 [IRR12009] . A program compares every quotation from these five sources with the text. Of Volume I, I read the chapters on procedure and the worked examples, and not the chapters on single accounting standards. Read through a tool that returns a summary of each page with short quotations: all other sources, among them the release rules of FY 2026, the Budget Call, the reporting circular, the circulars on BTMS and on payment through the bank, Book VI of the Administrative Code [EO292-B6] , and the resolutions of the GPPB of 2025 and 2026 with the forms of the procurement plans ( chapter 06, section 3.1 ). What is well supported: the constitutional rules, the release rules of FY 2026, the Budget Call of FY 2027, the procurement law and its complete rules, the steps from the obligation to the payment with the forms and the certificates, the records of each unit of an agency and the accounting entries, the rules on cash advances and on transfers between agencies, the property records, the powers of COA and the liability of officers in the Auditing Code, the reporting circular, the structure of UACS and the chain of numbers on the forms, the BTMS circular, the functions of BTr, the sections of the Local Government Code that are cited, the Partnership Code, the national disaster fund of FY 2026, and the assessment scores. What is mostly from general knowledge: the steps inside each chamber of Congress, the internal work of BIR and BOC and the reports of the collecting banks, the auctions of government securities, the steps of appointment of personnel, the steps of a tax refund and of a cash aid program, the present practice of audit reports, and what the servicing bank checks before it pays. Four limits concern the sources that I read as files. The Manual is of 2015. I checked one later change, the threshold of PHP 50,000 for property, and I did not search for others. The Manual was written under the earlier procurement law, so its examples of a works contract use the percentages of that time. The file of the Implementing Rules is the text of February 2025. The list of the resolutions of the GPPB to 14 August 2026 contains no amendment of a section, as far as the titles show, and I read the guidelines that the GPPB added only as summaries. And a rule in a manual shows what must be done. It does not show what agencies do. For practice the atlas has only the scores and short statements of the assessment of 2025. Two more limits are as before. Executive Order No. 126 of 2026 and the state of the FY 2027 budget bill are known to me only from press releases and press reports. Rules that are set each year are given for fiscal year 2026 or 2027. Reference F lists every source with its address and the way it was read, and in section 5 the decisions that shape the atlas. Reference G lists 86 numbered points: 18 differences between sources, and 68 facts that I could not verify or could verify only in part. 5 of these facts are settled, 15 are settled in part, and 48 are open. A difference between sources is a place where two official texts, or two places of the same text, say different things. The atlas states both sides of each and does not decide.

t: 01. Planning and investment programming
x: Part of the Philippine PFM Atlas. Facts as of 8 October 2026. The codes in the column "Basis" are explained in Reference F . "GK" means general knowledge that I did not open in a source during this work.

t: 1. The question this process answers
x: Which programs and projects may ask for money in the budget, and who decided that they are priorities?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
x: The budget covers one year. A road, a school program or an information system takes several years. The government therefore keeps plans for several years, and the budget of each year is meant to pay for one slice of those plans. The plans form a chain. A development plan states goals for six years. An investment program lists the programs and projects that serve those goals, with their cost per year. Large projects are appraised one by one before they may be funded. Only then does a project appear in a budget proposal. A case where the chain works: an agency lists a project in the investment program, obtains the required approvals, and proposes it in the budget as a new project (Tier 2, see chapter 03 ). The budget examiner can see that the project was planned and approved. A case where the chain fails: an item enters the budget during legislation and was never in the investment program. The PFM Reforms Roadmap reports this as a gap: additions by Congress without regional consultation, ceilings that arrive late, and no single system that follows a proposal from plan to budget [ROADMAP2024] . Terms used in this chapter. The Philippine Development Plan (PDP) is the medium-term plan, now for 2023 to 2028. The Public Investment Program (PIP) is the list of priority programs and projects of all agencies for the same period. The Three-Year Rolling Infrastructure Program (TRIP) is the infrastructure part of that list for three years, extended by one year each year. PIPOL is the DEPDev web system in which agencies enter these programs and projects.

t: 02. The fiscal framework
x: Part of the Philippine PFM Atlas. Facts as of 8 October 2026. The codes in the column "Basis" are explained in Reference F . "GK" means general knowledge that I did not open in a source during this work.

t: 1. The question this process answers
x: How large may the budget be in total, and who decides this before any agency writes a proposal?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
x: The total of the budget is not the sum of what agencies ask for. It is decided first, from the top, by one committee. Agencies then receive a share of that total. The decision follows from three numbers that depend on each other. If the government expects a certain revenue and accepts a certain deficit, the total it may spend is fixed: spending = revenue + deficit. The deficit must be financed, so the amount to borrow follows: borrowing = deficit + repayment of old debt that matures in the year, adjusted for any change in the cash balance. A case where this works: revenue is collected as forecast, and agencies receive cash authority for all their allotments. A case where this fails: revenue is lower than forecast. The total of allotments was already fixed by the budget law, but the cash is not there. The government must then borrow more, or DBM must slow the issue of cash authority (see chapter 11 ). This is why an agency can hold an allotment and still be unable to pay. Terms used in this chapter. The Development Budget Coordination Committee (DBCC) is the committee that recommends these numbers. The fiscal program is the set of numbers for one year: revenue, disbursements, deficit and financing. The Executive Technical Board is the group of senior officials that prepares the work of the DBCC.

t: 3. Authorities and their roles
x: Authority Role in this process Basis DBCC Recommends to the Cabinet and the President: the level of the annual expenditure program and the ceilings, the split between current operating expenditures and capital outlays, the reliability of revenue estimates, tax measures, and the level of borrowing DBCC-PAGE DBM Secretary Chairs the DBCC DBCC-PAGE Secretary of Finance Co-chairperson of the DBCC since Administrative Order No. 37 of 13 August 2025 (with effect from 27 April 2025). DOF brings the revenue forecast AO37 DEPDev Member. Brings the growth targets and the economic outlook DBCC-PAGE . Content of its input: GK Office of the President Member DBCC-PAGE , AO37 , EO108 BSP Resource institution, not a member DBCC-PAGE Executive Technical Board Prepares and clears the papers of the DBCC DBCC-PAGE BIR and BOC Give the collection forecasts and receive collection targets GK BTr Gives the debt service estimates and the financing options. Uses the fiscal program for its cash forecast and its borrowing plan EO449 , BTR-SITE Cabinet and President Approve the fiscal program DBCC-PAGE History of the DBCC, as stated on the DBM page: it was created on 14 May 1970 by Executive Order No. 232 as the Presidential Development Budget Committee, was renamed in 1972, and has its present composition under Executive Order No. 292 of 1987 [DBCC-PAGE] . The rule in that order, the Administrative Code, is its section on budget levels. The budget department, the finance department, the planning authority and the central bank recommend to the President, within the committee, the total levels of revenue, expenditure and debt. The section also states two limits. "The ordinary income of government shall be used primarily to provide appropriations for current operations." And no appropriation may be proposed "unless the amount involved is covered by the ordinary income, or unless it is supported by a proposal creating additional sources of funds or revenue, including those generated from domestic and foreign borrowings, sufficient to cover the same" [EO292-B6 s.13] . I read this section through a summary with quotations.

t: 03. Budget preparation
x: Part of the Philippine PFM Atlas. Facts as of 8 October 2026. The codes in the column "Basis" are explained in Reference F . "GK" means general knowledge that I did not open in a source during this work.

t: 1. The question this process answers
x: How does the Executive turn the total of the fiscal program and the requests of all agencies into one proposed budget for Congress?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
x: Two things must be reconciled. From the top, the DBCC fixes the total that may be spent ( chapter 02 ). From below, each agency states what it needs. The method that reconciles them is called the Two-Tier Budgeting Approach . The method first fixes the cost of what the government already does. This is Tier 1 . The Budget Call defines it as the "estimated cash requirements for ongoing program, activity, projects (P/A/Ps) and commitments at the same scope and quality" [NBM156] . Tier 1 is based on the Forward Estimates , which are the costs of ongoing programs for the next three years, formulated by DBM together with each agency. What remains under the ceiling is the fiscal space . The Budget Call defines it as "the difference between the projected expenditure program (after considering projected revenues and deficit targets) and Tier 1" [NBM156] . Only this amount is available for new or expanded programs and projects. These are Tier 2 proposals, and they compete with each other. A case where the method works: an agency continues a program at the same scale. Its cost is in the Forward Estimates and passes into Tier 1 with little discussion. The discussion can then concentrate on new proposals. A case where the method fails: the Forward Estimates are too high because a program was under-spent in earlier years. Tier 1 then takes space that is not needed, and good new proposals are refused. A second case of failure is outside the method: an item is added during legislation and never passed through either tier. The law gives the general rules of this stage. Each head of an agency submits its request for appropriations "in accordance with the budget calendar, format, and such rules and regulations as may be issued", with its objectives, its link to the development plans, its expected results and unit costs, its staffing and its contingent liabilities [EO292-B6 s.14] . The proposals are to be judged "on the basis of their own merits and not on the basis of a given percentage or peso increase or decrease from a prior year's budget level", and each activity, new or ongoing, "using a zero-base approach" [EO292-B6 s.16] . The two-tier method is the present way of DBM to apply these rules: Tier 1 accepts the cost of ongoing work from the Forward Estimates, and Tier 2 examines new work on its merits. Whether Tier 1 meets the words of the law on a zero-base approach is a question that I leave open. I read these sections through summaries with quotations. Other terms. The Budget Call is the DBM memorandum that starts the process. BP forms are the Budget Preparation forms that agencies complete. OSBPS is the Online Submission of Budget Proposals System of DBM. The National Expenditure Program (NEP) is the detailed proposed budget. The Budget of Expenditures and Sources of Financing (BESF) contains the fiscal tables.

t: 1. The question this process answers
x: How does the proposed budget become a law, what may Congress and the President each change, and what happens if no law is passed in time?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
x: The Constitution contains one rule from which the whole process follows: "No money shall be paid out of the Treasury except in pursuance of an appropriation made by law" [CONST VI.29(1)] . An appropriation is this permission in a law. The yearly law that contains most appropriations is the General Appropriations Act (GAA) . The powers are divided. The President proposes. Congress may reduce or rearrange but may not increase the appropriations recommended by the President for the operation of the government as specified in the budget [CONST VI.25(1)] . The President then signs, and may reject single items while approving the rest. This is the item veto [CONST VI.27(2)] . A case where the process works: the bill is passed and signed before 1 January, and execution starts on the first day of the fiscal year. A case where it fails: no bill is passed by the end of the year. The Constitution then keeps the government running: the law of the preceding year is deemed re-enacted and stays in force until the new bill is passed [CONST VI.25(7)] . This happened for four days at the start of 2026. The FY 2025 law was deemed re-enacted until 4 January 2026, and the FY 2026 law, Republic Act No. 12314, took effect on 5 January 2026 [NBC599] . A long period of re-enactment causes problems: new programs have no appropriation, and programs that ended still have one (GK). Terms. The General Appropriations Bill (GAB) is the budget in the form of a bill. The bicameral conference committee is the group of members of both chambers that reconciles their two versions. The enrolled bill is the final text sent to the President.

t: 1. The question this process answers
x: The budget law is in force. What must an agency hold before it may sign a contract, and what must it hold before it may pay?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
x: An appropriation in the law does not yet allow an agency to act. Two further authorities are needed, and they are separate. The first is the allotment . It allows the agency to commit the government, for example to sign a contract or to hire. A commitment of this kind is called an obligation . An allotment contains no cash. The Administrative Code defines the allotment as "an authorization issued by the Department of the Budget to an agency, which allows it to incur obligations for specified amounts contained in a legislative appropriation" [EO292-B6 s.2] . The second is the cash authority . Its main form is the Notice of Cash Allocation (NCA) . It is a limit: the largest amount that the agency may pay from its account at a servicing bank in a period. The accounting manual says: "The NCA specifies the maximum amount of withdrawal that an entity can make from a government bank for the period indicated" [GAM-V1 Ch.5 s.38] . The agency does not receive cash. The bank pays on the agency's order up to the limit, and the Treasury then repays the bank ( chapter 07 ). Why two authorities? Because they answer two different questions. The allotment answers "may the government make this commitment this year?", and the answer comes from the budget law. The cash authority answers "is there cash to pay this month?", and the answer comes from the cash position of the Treasury ( chapter 11 ). A case where the system works: an agency holds an allotment for a contract, the supplier delivers in June, and the NCA of the second quarter covers the payment. A case where it fails: the supplier delivers on 28 June, the voucher is approved on 2 July, and the unused part of the second-quarter NCA lapsed on 30 June. The agency holds a valid obligation and an approved claim, and still cannot pay until a new NCA is issued. In the budget reports this claim appears as an unpaid obligation that is due and demandable. Other terms. A Special Allotment Release Order (SARO) is the document by which DBM releases an allotment that needs clearance. A General Allotment Release Order (GARO) releases an allotment to all agencies for one common purpose. GAA as allotment order means that for items without conditions the law itself is the allotment and no document is issued. A Special Budget Request is the request of the agency for a SARO. An operating unit is an entity that receives release documents directly from DBM.

The President may suspend the expenditure of allotted funds, except for the pay of permanent staff EO292-B6 s.37, s.38 No obligation and no payment without the certificate of the chief accountant that funds are available and that the allotment can be charged EO292-B6 s.40, PD1445 s.86 Heads of agencies "shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments". t: 06. Procurement
x: Part of the Philippine PFM Atlas. Facts as of 8 October 2026. t: 1. The question this process answers
x: When an agency needs goods, works or services from the private sector, how does it choose the supplier, and how is this choice linked to the budget?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
x: An agency may not buy from a supplier of its own choice without a procedure. The law requires a procedure in which suppliers compete under rules announced in advance, and in which a committee, not one person, decides. The general procedure is competitive bidding . Ten other modes exist for defined situations. Procurement and the budget run at the same time, and the award needs a result from both. The agency may plan and even conduct the bidding before the budget law is in force. This is early procurement . But the law says: "No award of contract shall be made until the approval and effectivity of the appropriate funding" [RA12009 s.12] . A case where the procedure works: the item is in the procurement plan, the bidding is done in the last months of the year before, the budget law takes effect in January, and the contract is awarded in the same month. The agency has the whole year for delivery and payment. A case where it fails: the bidding starts only after the allotment is released, and it fails twice because no bidder qualifies. The contract is signed in November. Delivery cannot be completed and accepted within the validity of the appropriation, and the money reverts. The budget records of the agency show an unobligated or unpaid amount, and nothing in those records says that the cause was in procurement. Terms. The head of the procuring entity is the official who approves plans and awards, for an agency its head or an authorized official. The Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) conducts the procedure. The Annual Procurement Plan (APP) lists all procurement of the year. PhilGEPS is the electronic procurement portal. The approved budget for the contract is the ceiling for bids on one contract.

t: 3. The law and its rules
x: Fact Basis The law is Republic Act No. 12009, the New Government Procurement Act, of 20 July 2024. It repealed Republic Act No. 9184, with a transition period of three years RA12009 s.115 It covers goods, infrastructure projects and consulting services, from any source of funds, for national agencies, state universities, government corporations, government financial institutions and local governments RA12009 s.4 Its Implementing Rules are GPPB Resolution No. 02-2025 of 4 February 2025, published in the Official Gazette on 10 February 2025, in effect since 25 February 2025. A GPPB advisory of 31 July 2026 tells procuring entities to "use and cite only" this text GPPB-ADV I read the complete Implementing Rules, sections 1 to 117, in the text that was published on 10 February 2025. Where the Act and the Rules give different numbers of days or add conditions, the Rules decide the practice IRR12009 The Rules leave the details of each mode and of contract implementation to guidelines, manuals and standard forms of the GPPB. The standard forms were due within ninety days after the approval of the Rules, and procuring entities have a transition period of three years from the approval of the forms. Section 3.1 lists what the GPPB approved until 14 August 2026 IRR12009 s.26.2, s.71.1.6, s.112.3, s.113.3 Did the GPPB change the Rules after February 2025? The list of its resolutions to 14 August 2026 contains no resolution that amends a section of the Rules, as far as the titles show. Several resolutions add guidelines, and they declare some of these guidelines to be appendices or annexes of the Rules. One resolution of 6 October 2025 speaks of "proposed amendments" of the Rules that were then under review. I did not find a resolution that approves them GPPB-LIST , GPPB2025-11 Which law applies to an older procurement: Republic Act No. 9184 and its rules "shall be applicable in all procurement projects published prior to the effectivity of the IRR", which is 25 February 2025 GPPB2025-05 The standard forms were approved on 14 May 2025 and published on 23 June 2025. Their use is mandatory since 21 September 2025. The transition period of three years is counted from the approval of the forms: it "commenced on 14 May 2025", and procuring entities are "given until 15 May 2028" to comply fully. For a subject on which the GPPB has not yet issued a new guideline or form, entities may continue to use the one of the earlier law GPPB2025-03 , GPPB2025-05 A different document must not be used: the "Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 12009 (1st Edition, as of 31 March 2026)", which the technical office of the GPPB had published. t: 3.2 A rule for a limited time: the election period of 2026
x: Elections of barangay officials and of youth councils are held on 2 November 2026. The election period is "from 3 October 2026 to 9 November 2026". Rule Dates Procuring entities may continue their procurement activities The whole election period No release, disbursement or expenditure of public funds, "specifically the issuance of a Notice of Award", for public works and housing-related projects and for social welfare and services projects 18 September to 1 November 2026 Exceptions for public works, among them: maintenance without additional laborers, contracts awarded before 18 September 2026, preparatory work done before that date, some ongoing and foreign-assisted projects that are listed with the Commission on Elections, and emergency repair after a calamity. Routine expenses are an exception for social welfare and housing projects. The summary that I read gives more conditions for each exception The same dates Named programs of cash aid are "absolutely prohibited", except burial and medical assistance 23 October to 2 November 2026 No construction or maintenance of roads and bridges that are paid from barangay funds 23 October to 1 November 2026 A request for an exemption goes to the Commission on Elections, not to the GPPB The circular names as its basis section 261, paragraphs (v) and (w), of the Omnibus Election Code and two resolutions of the Commission on Elections of 2026. I did not open them. What this means for the main model: the rule stops the notice of award, which ends the choice of the supplier, and the release of money, for a part of the budget and for about six weeks. The body that can grant an exemption is outside PFM. A forecast of awards and payments for the fourth quarter of 2026 that does not know this rule will expect acts that the law does not allow in these weeks (Inference). What I could not read: how the circular treats a payment that is due in this period on a contract that was awarded before it, for projects other than public works. The summary did not state it.

Condition Section The agency may start, but may not award, for goods, works or consulting services to be delivered in the next fiscal year, once the President's budget (or the local expenditure program, or the proposed corporate budget) is submitted 12.1 The head of the procuring entity must have approved the indicative Annual Procurement Plan 12.2 The budget for the contract may not exceed the amount in the indicative plan 12.3 No award until the funding is approved and in effect, and until the head of the procuring entity has approved the final plan. t: Contracts for more than one year
x: An appropriation is valid for one year, but many contracts last longer. Diagram 06f shows what is needed. The question it answers: what allows an agency to sign one contract for several years, and where does the money of each year come from? The answer has two parts. The Multi-Year Contractual Authority (MYCA) is a permission of DBM to sign. The budget law of each year provides the money of that year. The first does not replace the second. Rule Basis A MYCA "or similar documents shall be required before Procuring Entities commence any procurement activity" for a multi-year contract paid from local funds. DBM issues it. Its total project cost is the basis of the budget for the contract IRR12009 s.9.1, s.5 The request states the total project cost and the period. With it: a certification by the head of agency that procurement has not started, a commitment to keep the yearly amounts inside the budget ceilings, a funding strategy and a medium-term expenditure program, and the approvals that the project needs CL2025-6 A MYCA cannot be changed after it is issued CL2025-6 The yearly amounts go into the Tier 1 budget proposal of the agency. DBM evaluates them by the capacity of the agency to implement CL2025-6 Note printed on the MYCA form: "the actual obligations to be incurred in any given fiscal year shall in no case exceed the cash appropriation" of that year CL2025-6 State universities, government corporations and government financial institutions: when the project is paid partly from their own income, approval of the governing board and a MYCA for the part paid from the budget law. When it is paid fully from own income, approval of the governing board only IRR12009 s.9.1, CL2025-6 Local governments: an equivalent authorization of the sanggunian IRR12009 s.9.1 Regular and recurring services, for example rent and telecommunications, no longer need a MYCA. Their contracts may be renewed if funds are available CL2025-6 , IRR12009 s.18 Projects financed by foreign loans do not need a MYCA before the contract is signed GMA-MYCA (press report of a DBM statement) A case where it works: a bridge of PHP 10 billion is planned as 3, 4 and 3 billion in three years. DBM issues a MYCA for 10 billion. The agency signs one contract, and each budget law contains the amount of its year (example given by DBM [GMA-MYCA] ). A case where it fails: the budget law of the second year contains 2 billion, not 4. The MYCA is still valid, but the agency may obligate only 2 billion in that year. No source that I read says what the agency must then do with the contract (Inference).

t: Framework agreements
x: The question: how can an agency fix the supplier and the prices now, when it does not know yet how much it will need, or when? The Rules allow a framework agreement . It is "in the nature of an option contract" that states the terms of later contracts with one supplier or with several, "subject to the guidelines to be issued by the GPPB" [IRR12009 s.16] . The agency receives a right to order. It has no duty to order. The GPPB approved the guidelines on 23 July 2026. Diagram 06g shows the order of the acts. Rule of the guidelines Basis The agreement is procured by competitive bidding or by limited source bidding, for goods, infrastructure projects or consulting services GPPB2026-12 Its period is fixed at one, two or three years and cannot be extended GPPB2026-12 No Multi-Year Contractual Authority is needed before the agreement. The amount that is needed in each year must be in the approved budget of that year GPPB2026-12 The certificate of availability of funds (CAF) "shall not be required prior to the execution of a Framework Agreement." GPPB2026-12 An order under the agreement is named a Call-Off. It is the purchase order by which the agency uses its option. "The issuance of the CAF shall be required for every Call-Off." GPPB2026-12 The contract for a delivery is perfected at each Call-Off, not at the agreement. The price of the option is PHP 1.00 GPPB2026-12 When an agreement of more than one year has several suppliers, a competition among them, named a Mini Competition, comes before each Call-Off GPPB2026-12 All Call-Offs together stay within the maximum quantity or the total contract price of the agreement. The Call-Offs of one year stay within the approved budget for the contract GPPB2026-12 What this changes in the main model. For an ordinary contract the certificate of funds comes once, before the contract ( chapter 07 ). For a framework agreement it comes before each order. The form of the purchase order in the Manual has the place for this certificate, with the number, the date and the amount of the obligation request [GAM-V2 App.61] . The atlas concludes that the obligation is recorded for each Call-Off, and that the agreement itself is not an obligation in the budget records. This is an inference: I read the guidelines as a summary, and the summary does not name the obligation request. A case where it works: a hospital needs medicines during the whole year and cannot say in January how many. It signs an agreement with fixed unit prices. In each quarter it orders what it needs, and each order has its own certificate of funds, within the allotment of that time. A case where it fails: the need arises when the allotment is fully obligated, or before it is released. No certificate can be issued, so no Call-Off can be made, although the agreement is valid. The agreement gave the agency a supplier and prices. It did not give it money (Inference from the two rules on the certificate).

t: Diagram 06e  States of one contract, from award to closing
x: Code file: ../diagrams/mermaid/06e_contract_implementation.mmd . Rendered image: ../rendered/06e_contract_implementation.png . Question: after the award, through which states does a contract pass, which events remove it from the normal path, and which limit applies to each event? How to read it: the middle line is the normal path. The states on the sides are the exits and the returns. An arrow without text that returns to "In performance" means that the work continues. Short labels: "change within the limit" = an amendment to order (goods) or a variation order (works) of not more than 10 percent of the original contract price, or up to 20 percent with the approval of the head of the procuring entity. "allowed reason" = a reason for suspension or extension that the rules allow. "date passed" = the completion date passed: for each day of delay, damages of one tenth of one percent of the cost of the part that is not performed. "legal ground" = default of the contractor, convenience of the procuring entity (for example when the funding is withheld), unlawful acts, or an event beyond control. The advance: for works, an advance of not more than 15 percent of the contract price, only on the written request of the contractor and against an irrevocable standby letter of credit, a bank guarantee or a surety bond. For goods: 15 percent against a letter of credit or bank guarantee of the same amount. Diagram 07i follows the amounts. Sources: the Implementing Rules of Republic Act No. 12009, text published on 10 February 2025 [IRR12009] : award, contract and securities ss.66-69. Amendment to order and variation order s.71.1.1, s.71.2.1. Suspension and extension s.71.1.2, s.71.2.2, s.71.2.3. Liquidated damages s.71.1.4, s.71.2.4, s.97. Advance payment s.71.1.5, s.71.2.5. Progress payment and retention money s.71.2.7, s.71.2.8. Termination s.71.4. Warranty s.90. Sanctions ss.98-105. Period for the notice to proceed [RA12009 s.66] . Multi-year contracts need a Multi-Year Contractual Authority [IRR12009 s.9] [CL2025-6] . No payment before a certificate that the delivery was inspected and accepted, except an approved advance [PD1445 s.88] . A difference inside the rules: for goods, the damages are counted on the cost of the delayed goods [IRR12009 s.71.1.4] . The general rule counts them on the cost of the unperformed portion [IRR12009 s.97] . Limit: later amendments of the Rules are not in the text that I read. The Rules leave other details of contract implementation to manuals of the GPPB, which I did not open [IRR12009 s.71.1.6] .

t: Diagram 06f  A contract that lasts more than one year: the Multi-Year Contractual Authority (MYCA)
x: Code file: ../diagrams/mermaid/06f_multi_year_contracts.mmd . Rendered image: ../rendered/06f_multi_year_contracts.png . Question: an appropriation is valid for one year, but a bridge takes three years to build. What allows an agency to sign one contract for the whole work, and where does the money of each year come from? Idea: two different permissions are needed. The MYCA allows the agency to SIGN a contract for more than one year. The budget law of each year provides the MONEY of that year. The first does not replace the second. How to read it: top = which authorization is needed, by source of money. Middle = from the MYCA to the contract. Bottom frame = what is repeated in every year of the contract. Sources: the MYCA is defined as the authority to procure multi-year projects in the form and under the conditions set by DBM [IRR12009 s.5] . It is required before any procurement activity for locally funded multi-year contracts, DBM issues it, and its total project cost is the basis of the Approved Budget for the Contract. The cases by source of money: sections 9.1.1 to 9.1.4 [IRR12009 s.9] . Request documents, no change after issue, yearly amounts in the Tier 1 proposal, the note on the form about yearly obligations, and the rule that regular and recurring services no longer need a MYCA [CL2025-6] . DBM issues the MYCA under the cash budgeting order [EO91] . Renewal of contracts for regular and recurring services when funds are available [IRR12009 s.18] . From a press report of a DBM statement [GMA-MYCA] : the example of a bridge of PHP 10 billion programmed at 3, 4 and 3 billion in three years, and the statement that projects financed by foreign loans do not need a MYCA before the contract is signed. Inference: the grey box at the bottom. No source that I read says what the agency does when the budget law of a year contains less than the amount planned for that year.

t: Diagram 06g  A framework agreement: funds are certified before each order, not before the agreement
x: Code file: ../diagrams/mermaid/06g_framework_agreement.mmd . Rendered image: ../rendered/06g_framework_agreement.png . Question: an agency fixes a supplier and prices now, and does not know yet how much it will buy, or when. At which moment must funds be certified, and at which moment is the government bound to pay? Idea: the agreement gives the agency a right to order and no duty to order. Each order is a separate purchase order, named a Call-Off, and each one needs its own certificate of funds. In the main model of the atlas, the allotment and the award meet in a contract. Here they meet once for every order, and not at the agreement. How to read it: top = the agreement, which is made once. Green frame = what is repeated for every order. Purple boxes = rules of the agreement. Grey boxes = two inferences of mine. Sources: the framework agreement as an option contract, subject to guidelines of the GPPB [IRR12009 s.16] . The guidelines of 23 July 2026: the modes by which the agreement is procured, the period of one to three years, no Multi-Year Contractual Authority, no certificate of funds before the agreement, a certificate for every Call-Off, the Call-Off as the purchase order, the competition among several suppliers, the limits of quantity and price, the price of the option [GPPB2026-12] . The form of the purchase order, with the place for the certificate and for the number of the obligation request [GAM-V2 App.61] . Limit: I read the guidelines through a tool that returned a summary with short quotations, not the full text. The guidelines take effect 15 days after their publication. I did not read the date of publication. Inference: the two grey boxes. First, that the obligation is recorded when the certificate for an order is issued. Second, that no Call-Off can be made when funds are not available. The summary of the guidelines does not name the obligation request. Example: the example in the first box is mine. It is not from a source.

t: 07. Obligation, verification and payment
x: Part of the Philippine PFM Atlas. Facts as of 8 October 2026. The codes in the column "Basis" are explained in Reference F . "GK" means general knowledge that I did not open in a source during this work.

t: 1. The question this process answers
x: For one payment to a supplier: which officer states which fact, in which document, which record is written at each step, and through which accounts does the money move? And what replaces the contract and the accepted delivery in the other kinds of payment? The main source of this chapter is the Government Accounting Manual for National Government Agencies of 2015: Volume I for the procedures and the entries [GAM-V1] , Volume II for the forms [GAM-V2] . Where a later rule changed the Manual, the chapter gives the later rule and says so.

t: 2. The idea in plain words
x: A payment is the last act of several lines of work that run at the same time. Three things must each be true before money may leave, and each is made true by a different party. The government is committed, within its authority. The agency holds an allotment and has recorded an obligation against it. The head of the budget unit states this in Box B of the obligation request [GAM-V2 App.11] . The other party has a claim. For a purchase: the goods, services or works were delivered, inspected and accepted. Two officers state this in the acceptance report, each for one fact [GAM-V2 App.62] . The accounting unit then records a payable. The budget reports call such an amount due and demandable [JC2019-1] . Other kinds of payment have another event in this place (section 7.1). Cash may be used. The agency holds a cash authority (NCA) with enough balance. The head of accounting states this in Box C of the voucher, after a look into the registry of the NCA [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] [GAM-V2 App.32] . Diagram 07b shows these three meeting points. A drawing with one line of steps hides them, and this is the main reason why the process is hard to see as a whole. A record is written at each of these moments. The obligation enters a registry. The accepted delivery produces a journal entry for the payable. The certified voucher is entered in the registry of the NCA. The payment order produces a journal entry for the payment. No record waits for the end of the process. Diagram 07a names the record at each step. A case where the process works: the three facts are all true in the same month, and the supplier is paid within days after acceptance. A case where it fails: the delivery is accepted and the payable is recorded, but the NCA of the quarter has lapsed or is fully used. The head of accounting cannot sign Box C. The Manual says that he or she "notes that cash is not yet available" and that the voucher is kept [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] . The claim is valid and stays unpaid. The reverse failure also exists: cash authority is available but the delivery is not accepted before the quarter ends, and the cash authority lapses unused. A case where two meeting points occur on one day: for many regular expenses, for example a utility bill, the obligation request reaches the budget unit together with the voucher [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] . The obligation is then recorded on the day on which the claim is examined. For a purchase with a contract or a purchase order, the obligation is recorded before the order is signed, because the order carries the number of the obligation request [GAM-V2 App.61] . A case where the first meeting point occurs many times for one procurement: under a framework agreement the supplier and the prices are fixed first, and no certificate of funds is needed for the agreement. A certificate is needed for each order under it. The guidelines of the GPPB of July 2026 name such an order a Call-Off [GPPB2026-12] . Chapter 06, section 5 , and diagram 06g give the rules. Terms. The Obligation Request and Status (ORS) is the document that charges an amount to an allotment. The disbursement voucher (DV) is the document that approves one claim for payment. Accounts payable are "valid and legal obligations" of an agency "for which, goods/services/projects have been delivered/rendered/completed and accepted". The LDDAP-ADA (List of Due and Demandable Accounts Payable with Advice to Debit Account) is the payment order to the bank: a list of creditors with the amounts, and below it an instruction to the bank to debit the account of the agency. The Modified Disbursement System (MDS) is the arrangement in which servicing banks pay on agency orders and the Treasury repays the banks. A journal entry voucher (JEV) records one transaction in the accounting books. The registry of the NCA (in the Manual: Registry of Allotments and Notice of Cash Allocation, RANCA) is the list in which the accounting unit compares the allotments received, the NCAs received and the NCAs used [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.2, s.3] .
