The Auditing Code says: "Except with the prior approval of the President (Prime Minister) the government shall not be obliged to make an advance payment for services not yet rendered or for supplies and materials not yet delivered under any contract therefor" [PD1445 s.88] . An order of the President of 2011 gave this approval for goods under the earlier procurement law [MO15-2011] . The Implementing Rules of the procurement law of 2024 name the following cases [IRR12009 s.71] . Subject Goods Works (infrastructure projects) Basis Advance payment Not more than 15 percent of the contract amount, against an irrevocable letter of credit or bank guarantee of the same amount, paid within 60 days from the signing of the contract. Also 15 percent for goods needed in an area under a declared state of calamity. A single advance of not more than 50 percent for hotel and restaurant services, the use of conference areas and the lease of office space, where a down payment is standard practice Not more than 15 percent of the total contract price, in one amount or at most two instalments. Only on the written request of the contractor, and against an irrevocable standby letter of credit, a bank guarantee, or a surety bond callable upon demand IRR12009 s.71.1.5, s.71.2.5 Recovery of the advance "All progress payments shall first be charged against the advance payment until the latter has been fully exhausted" A part of the advance is deducted from each progress payment IRR12009 s.71.1.5, s.71.2.7 Progress payment Once a month the contractor may submit a statement of work accomplished. The representative or engineer of the agency checks it and certifies the amount. Materials and equipment that were delivered to the site and are not yet part of the works are not paid, unless the instructions to bidders say otherwise IRR12009 s.71.2.7 Retention money For the warranty: 1 to 5 percent of every progress payment, or a special bank guarantee of 1 to 5 percent of the contract price. Released after the warranty period: at least three months for expendable supplies and one year for other supplies 10 percent of the amount due before any deduction, from every progress payment until 50 percent of the works are completed. No further retention after that when the work is satisfactory and on schedule. Due for release upon final acceptance IRR12009 s.90.1, s.71.2.8 Damages for delay One tenth of one percent of the cost of the delayed goods for every day. When the total reaches 10 percent of the contract price, the agency may rescind At least one tenth of one percent of the cost of the unperformed portion for every day. The same limit of 10 percent IRR12009 s.71.1.4, s.71.2.4, s.97 Change of the contract Amendment to order: an increase of not more than 10 percent of the original price, or 20 percent with approval of the head of the procuring entity Variation orders: not more than 10 percent in total, in exceptional cases up to 20 percent IRR12009 s.71.1.1, s.71.2.1 Late payment by the agency The contractor may suspend the work when a certified progress billing is unpaid for more than 45 days IRR12009 s.71.2.2 Performance security, before the contract is signed 5 percent of the contract price in cash or bank instruments, or 30 percent as surety bond 10 percent in cash or bank instruments, or 30 percent as surety bond IRR12009 s.68 A case where the exception works: a contractor needs money to bring equipment to the site. t: 11. Timing
x: A claim becomes payable when the delivery is accepted. It can be paid only while the NCA of the quarter has balance. The first NCA of FY 2026 covers the first quarter. Unused regular NCA lapses on the last working day of the quarter [NBC599] . The bank must credit the payees within the next two banking days after it receives the payment order with its summary list [CL2018-14] . In the electronic facility of LBP, payees are credited within 24 to 48 hours after the agency approves the payment order [eMDS] . Tax withheld is remitted by the 10th day of the following month [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.62] . Each month the agency reports its payments by type of authority in FAR 4, by the 10th day of the next month [JC2019-1] . The bank reconciliation is prepared within ten days from the receipt of the monthly bank statement and submitted within twenty days [GAM-V1 Ch.21] .

t: 12. When a step fails
x: Sections 4 to 7 describe the path when every check succeeds. Diagram 07g shows what happens when a check fails. The question it answers: who acts, where does the transaction continue, and in which record can a reader see the failure? The idea: each failure leads to a different next step. Some failures stop it before any record is made (rows 1 and 3). Some leave an obligation or a transfer that remains unsettled for months (rows 2, 4 and 8). Some end an authority (row 7). Two concern a payment that is already ordered or made (rows 5, 6 and 9). A model of the process that contains only the main path cannot represent unpaid obligations, lapsed authority or recovered payments. No. What fails Who acts, and how Where the transaction continues Record that shows it Basis 1 No allotment balance for the obligation request The budget unit refuses the request. In BTMS the system blocks an obligation above the allotment The agency asks for a change of allotment or for a new release ( diagram 05e ) Registry of allotments and obligations GAM-V1 Ch.3 s.10, NBC599 s.3.13, CL2025-8 2 The delivery is not accepted, or is late No acceptance report is issued. Items that do not conform are returned to the supplier. For delay the supplier owes damages of one tenth of one percent of the cost of the delayed goods for every day When the damages reach 10 percent of the contract price, the agency may rescind. Another supplier may then complete the contract, chosen by negotiated procurement The obligation stays open, or is changed by a notice of adjustment GAM-V1 Ch.8 s.15, IRR12009 s.71.1.4, s.35.3, GAM-V1 Ch.3 ss.13-14 3 The claim is incomplete, or was paid before The accounting unit returns the voucher. It finds an earlier payment in the index of payments The claimant completes the claim and submits it again Index of payments. No entry in the registry of the NCA GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12 4 No cash authority: the NCA is fully used, or the NCA of the quarter has lapsed The head of accounting cannot certify "Cash available". The voucher is kept. The agency requests an additional NCA from DBM If the claim is unpaid at the end of the year, it is a due and demandable obligation. A regular NCA of a later period also covers payables of earlier years Part C of the obligation request. When the decision is final and executory: a receivable in the books, and an order of execution against the persons liable ( diagram 09b ) Audit notices and statements COA2009-006 , GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.46 Row 4 is the most frequent case in the reports: the stock of expenditure arrears in 2023 was above 10 percent of expenditure [PEFA2025] . Diagram 08c explains why such an amount is an expense and a payable in the books, an obligation in the registry, and not yet a disbursement. A further case concerns accounts payable that stay unpaid for a long time. The Auditing Code lets COA revert to the General Fund any balance of accounts payable "which has been outstanding for two years or more and against which no actual claim, administrative or judicial, has been filed" [PD1445 s.98] .

t: Diagram 07a  From obligation to payment: who certifies what, and which record each step writes (goods bought by a national agency, paid by payment order)
x: Code file: ../diagrams/mermaid/07a_obligation_to_payment_sequence.mmd . Rendered image: ../rendered/07a_obligation_to_payment_sequence.png . Question: for one payment to a supplier, which officer certifies which fact, in which document, which record is written at each step, and which checks are made by someone outside the agency before the money leaves? What the diagram shows: every certification before step 20 is made by an officer of the agency itself. The first outside check is by the servicing bank (step 20). The bank checks the payment order and the cash limit. It does not check the delivery. COA examines after payment. The records are written during the process: the obligation at step 2, the payable at steps 7 and 8, the use of the cash authority at step 11, the payment at steps 27 and 28. Sources: the steps follow the Government Accounting Manual. Obligation [GAM-V1 Ch.3 s.15] . Delivery, inspection, acceptance and the entry for the payable [GAM-V1 Ch.8 s.15, Annex H] . Examination of the voucher, index of payments and registry of the NCA [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] . Payment order, its summary list, the copies and the daily report [GAM-V1 Ch.6 ss.50-57] . Tax withheld [GAM-V1 Ch.6 ss.60-62] . The wording of the certificates is that of the forms [GAM-V2 App.11, App.32, App.42, App.61, App.62] . Certificate of funds before a contract [PD1445 s.86] . Copy of the summary list to BTr and replenishment [CL2013-16A] . Electronic facility of the bank [eMDS] . Two banking days [CL2018-14] . Audit after payment [COA2011-002] . System controls of BTMS in the last note [BTMS-SITE] [CL2025-8] . Differences inside the sources: (1) the form of the voucher has five boxes, A to E [GAM-V2 App.32] . The text of the procedure calls the certificate of the accountant Box B and the approval Box C [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] . The diagram follows the form. (2) The worked example of the Manual records the payable at delivery [GAM-V1 Annex H] . Another section says that payables are recorded "based on approved DVs" [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.57] . The diagram follows the worked example. (3) The Manual lets the cashier certify the summary list [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.56] . The circular of 2013 names the head of accounting [CL2013-16A] . General knowledge, not opened in a source here: what the bank checks in step 20.

t: Diagram 07b  The three meeting points before a payment, and the record written at each step (national agency, contract for goods) (PlantUML)
x: Code file: ../diagrams/plantuml/07b_obligation_to_payment_swimlane.puml . Rendered image: ../rendered/07b_obligation_to_payment_swimlane.png . Question: which lines of work must BOTH be finished before the next step of a payment may happen, and which record does each unit write at its step? Idea: a payment needs three meetings. (1) An allotment and an award must both exist before the contract is signed and the obligation is recorded. (2) The obligation and an accepted delivery must both exist before the amount is a payable. (3) The claim in order and a cash authority (NCA) must both exist before the head of accounting certifies "cash available" on the voucher. The payment order follows the third meeting. How to read it: one column (lane) = one actor. A thick bar that opens = branches run in parallel. The thick bar that closes = ALL branches must be finished (AND-join). A line that starts with "Record:" names what is written at that step. Why PlantUML: Mermaid has no activity diagram with lanes and AND-joins. The Mermaid diagram 00d shows the same structure as a net without lanes. Where the meeting points are: the Manual places the check of the NCA at Box C of the voucher [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] , and its worked example records the payable at the accepted delivery [GAM-V1 Annex H] . Sources: [NBC599] allotment and NCA. [RA12009 s.12] no award before funding. [PD1445 s.86] certificate of funds before a contract. [GAM-V1 Ch.3 s.15] obligation. [GAM-V1 Ch.8 s.15] delivery, inspection, acceptance. [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12, s.56] voucher, registry of the NCA, payment order, daily report. [GAM-V2 App.11, App.32, App.42, App.62] wording of the forms. [GAM-V1 Annex H] entries of the agency and of the Treasury. [CL2013-16A] copy to BTr and replenishment. [COA2011-002] audit after payment. General knowledge (GK), not opened in a source here: what the bank checks before it debits the sub-account.

t: Diagram 07c  The chain of certifications for one payment: who signs, what the signature states, and who checks it
x: Code file: ../diagrams/mermaid/07c_voucher_certifications.mmd . Rendered image: ../rendered/07c_voucher_certifications.png . Question: a payment depends on several signatures. What exactly does each signature assert, and is that assertion checked by anyone outside the agency before the money leaves? How to read it: each row is one document. Left = who signs. Right = what the signature states, in the words of the form where the text is in quotation marks. The colour of the row shows who makes the statement: green = an officer of the agency, yellow = the bank, orange = the auditor. What the diagram shows: the facts "the goods were delivered" and "the delivery meets the order" are stated only by officers of the agency, and by two different officers. The bank checks the payment order. COA checks the substance, after payment. The officer who certifies that funds and cash are available (the accountant) is never the officer who signs the advice to the bank (the cashier). Sources: the words in quotation marks are read on the forms of the Manual: obligation request [GAM-V2 App.11] , purchase order [GAM-V2 App.61] , inspection and acceptance report [GAM-V2 App.62] , disbursement voucher [GAM-V2 App.32] , payment order [GAM-V2 App.42] . The seven basic requirements for a disbursement and the officer who certifies each [GAM-V1 Ch.2 s.36] . Certificate of funds before a contract [PD1445 s.86] [EO292-B6 s.40] . Signatories of the payment order, who must be bonded [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.51] . No member of the accounting unit or of the internal control unit may be designated to draw checks [PD1445 s.92] . Pre-audit by COA lifted in 2011, COA may restore it where internal control is inadequate [COA2011-002] . A difference inside the manual: the form of the voucher has five boxes, A to E. The text of the procedure calls the certificate of the accountant "Box B", the approval "Box C" and the receipt "Box D" [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] . This diagram follows the form. General knowledge, not opened in a source here: what the bank checks, and the role of the internal audit unit.

t: Diagram 07d  Payment and settlement: how money moves from the Treasury Single Account to the payee (Modified Disbursement System)
x: Code file: ../diagrams/mermaid/07d_payment_settlement_sequence.mmd . Rendered image: ../rendered/07d_payment_settlement_sequence.png . Question: the agency holds no cash for its regular budget. Through which accounts does the money pass when the agency pays, at which moment does cash leave the Treasury, and on which date does each party record the payment? Idea: under the Modified Disbursement System (MDS) the servicing bank pays first, from a fund that the Treasury keeps filled. The NCA is only a limit recorded at the bank. The Manual says of the account Cash-MDS in the books of the agency that "there is no actual cash with the GSBs" [GAM-V1 Ch.19 s.56] . Cash leaves the Treasury Single Account when BTr replenishes the bank for payments already made. Three dates for one payment: the agency credits its account Cash-MDS on the day of the daily report of payment orders issued. That report also contains payment orders that are not yet delivered to the bank [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.52, s.54] . The bank credits the payee 24 to 48 hours after it receives the payment order [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.2] . The Treasury records the subsidy to the agency when the bank has paid [GAM-V1 Annex H] . The monthly bank reconciliation explains the differences [GAM-V1 Ch.21] . Sources: NCA credited to MDS sub-accounts at LBP, DBP and PVB, lapsing at the end of the quarter [NBC599] . Receipt of the NCA in the books, no official receipt [GAM-V1 Ch.5 s.38] . Payment order, summary list, copies, same-day copy to BTr for the replenishment of the MDS Seed Fund, validated copy, invalidated items [GAM-V1 Ch.6 ss.50-56] [CL2013-16A] . Daily replenishment of servicing banks [PRIMER] . Electronic facility of LBP, adopted by a joint order of DBM and DOF of 12 March 2015 [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.58] [eMDS] . Checks, the daily advice of checks issued and cancelled, stale checks [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.2, s.12, s.44] . Bank reconciliation [GAM-V1 Ch.21] [PD1445 s.74] . Entry for the unused NCA [GAM-V1 Ch.19 s.55] . Treasury Single Account as a unified structure of government bank accounts [BTR-SITE] . Daily bank reconciliation in BTMS, payments by PESONet and InstaPay [BTMS-SITE] [CL2025-8] . General knowledge, not opened in a source here: steps 9 and 10 (the instruction to BSP and the entries at BSP).

t: Diagram 07f  States of one cash advance, from grant to liquidation
x: Code file: ../diagrams/mermaid/07f_cash_advance_states.mmd . Rendered image: ../rendered/07f_cash_advance_states.png . Question: a cash advance leaves the Treasury before any delivery is accepted. How does the government ensure that the money is later accounted for? Idea: a cash advance is money given to a named officer, who is personally accountable for it until he or she presents proof of how it was spent (liquidation) and returns the rest. In the books the money is a receivable from the officer until then, and not an expense. Sources: the three rules of the law: only for a legally authorized specific purpose, to be liquidated as soon as the purpose is served, and no new advance before the earlier one is settled [PD1445 s.89] . Bond, permanent appointment of disbursing officers, no transfer between officers [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.14] . Time limits: an advance for payroll within 5 days after the end of the pay period, local travel within 30 days after return, foreign travel within 60 days [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.15, ss.25-29] . Petty cash: replenished when 75 percent is used, never closed at the end of the year [GAM-V1 Ch.6 ss.35-39] . The accounts: Advances for Payroll, Advances to Officers and Employees, Advances for Operating Expenses, Advances to Special Disbursing Officer [GAM-V1 Ch.5 s.38, Ch.6 s.19] . A disallowance enters the books only when it is final and executory, as a receivable [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.46] . Bonding is administered by BTr [EO449] . Weakness reported: a part of the advances, in particular advances to government corporations, was not liquidated at the end of 2023 (indicator 27.3, score C) [PEFA2025] . General knowledge, not opened in a source here: the demand letter and the withholding of salary. They are in COA Circular No. 97-002, which the Manual names and which I did not open.

t: Diagram 07g  When a step fails: who acts, where the transaction continues, and which record shows it
x: Code file: ../diagrams/mermaid/07g_when_a_step_fails.mmd . Rendered image: ../rendered/07g_when_a_step_fails.png . Question: diagrams 07a and 07b show the path when every check succeeds. What happens when one check fails, and where can a reader of the records see that it failed? How to read it: each row is one kind of failure, in the order of the process. The rows are separate cases, not a sequence. Column 1 = what fails. Column 2 = who acts and how. Column 3 = where the transaction continues. Column 4 (grey) = the record or report in which the failure is visible. Why it matters for a process model: each row is a path that leaves the main sequence. A model that contains only the main sequence cannot represent unpaid obligations, lapsed authority or recovered payments. Sources: row 1, the registry balance is taken at every entry to prevent obligations above the allotment [GAM-V1 Ch.3 s.10] ; changes of allotment and their approval [NBC599 s.3.13] ; BTMS refuses an obligation above the allotment [CL2025-8] . Row 2, items that do not conform are returned to the supplier [GAM-V1 Ch.8 s.15] ; damages of one tenth of one percent of the cost of the delayed goods for every day of delay, and the right to rescind when they reach 10 percent of the contract price [IRR12009 s.71.1.4] ; take-over of an ended contract by negotiated procurement [IRR12009 s.35.3] ; notice of adjustment of an obligation [GAM-V1 Ch.3 ss.13-14] . Row 3, check of completeness and of the index of payments [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] . Row 4, the voucher is kept when the registry of the NCA shows no balance [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] ; a regular NCA lapses at the end of the quarter, additional NCAs, and the regular NCA covers payables of the current and of earlier years [NBC599 s.4.2] ; aging of unpaid obligations in FAR 3 and monthly disbursements in FAR 4 [JC2019-1] . Row 5, a payment order may be invalidated when the bank branch, the account name or the account number does not agree with the bank records; journal entry and new payment order [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.54] ; remarks of the bank [CL2018-14] . Row 6, stale checks and the entry that restores the payable [GAM-V1 Ch.6 ss.44-45] ; the law gives two years [PD1445 s.97] . Row 7, unused balances revert to the unappropriated surplus of the General Fund [NBC599 s.3.6] [EO292-B6 s.28] . Row 8, transfers are not disbursements until the receiver has used them for accepted deliveries [NBC599 s.3.4] ; reports of the receiver within ten days after each month and return of the unused balance [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.63] ; report FAR 1-C [JC2019-1] . Row 9, notices of suspension and of disallowance, appeal, finality, order of execution [COA2009-006] ; a disallowance enters the books only when it is final and executory [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.46] . Weakness reported: the stock of expenditure arrears in 2023 was above 10 percent of expenditure (indicator 22.1, score D) [PEFA2025] .

t: Diagram 07i  A works contract with an advance, progress billings and retention money (example of the Manual)
x: Code file: ../diagrams/mermaid/07i_advance_progress_retention.mmd . Rendered image: ../rendered/07i_advance_progress_retention.png . Question: when a contractor receives an advance and is then paid by progress billings, which amounts leave the Treasury on which occasion, what is retained, and what do the books show at each step? Idea: the advance is not a cost. It is money of the government in the hands of the contractor, covered by a security, and it is recovered from the later billings. A part of each payment is kept as retention money until final acceptance. Over the whole contract the payments, the retention and the tax together equal the contract price. The example: the amounts and the accounts are those of the worked example of the Manual for a building of PHP 800,000 [GAM-V1 Ch.10 s.8] . The Manual is of 2015 and its example follows the rules of that time. The rules of 2025: advance of not more than 15 percent, on the written request of the contractor and against an irrevocable standby letter of credit, a bank guarantee or a surety bond [IRR12009 s.71.2.5] . Progress billing not more often than once a month, checked and certified by the engineer of the agency. Deductions: work already paid, the part of the advance that is recovered, retention money, third-party liabilities, uncorrected defects [IRR12009 s.71.2.7] . Retention of 10 percent of the amount due before any deduction, from every progress payment until 50 percent of the works are completed, and released upon final acceptance [IRR12009 s.71.2.8] . Performance security before the contract is signed: 10 percent for works in cash or bank instruments, 30 percent as surety bond [IRR12009 s.68] . Damages for delay: at least one tenth of one percent of the cost of the unperformed portion for every day [IRR12009 s.71.2.4] . Defects liability period of one year from completion [IRR12009 s.90.2.2] . Differences between the example and the rules of 2025: (1) the example retains 10 percent of the payable after the advance is recovered (34,000). The rules of 2025 base the retention on the amount due before any deduction, and stop it after 50 percent of the works when the work is satisfactory and on schedule. (2) The performance security of the example is 75,000. Ten percent of the contract price would be 80,000. (3) The example computes the damages as one tenth of one percent of the contract. The rules of 2025 use the cost of the unperformed portion. Check of the arithmetic: cash to the contractor 120,000 + 282,200 + 282,200 + 68,000 = 752,400. Tax withheld 23,800 + 23,800 = 47,600. Together 800,000, the contract price.

t: 1. The question this process answers
x: Where is each event of budget execution recorded, by which unit and by which body, and how do these records become the reports that DBM, COA, BTr, Congress and the public receive? The main source of this chapter is the Government Accounting Manual for National Government Agencies of 2015: Volume I for the rules and the entries [GAM-V1] , Volume II for the forms [GAM-V2] , Volume III for the chart of accounts [GAM-V3] . The present list of budget reports is from the joint circular of 2019 [JC2019-1] , which is later than the Manual.

t: 2. The idea in plain words
x: No single record contains a whole transaction. Several units and bodies write about the same money, because each must answer a different question. Inside one agency there are two main sets of records. The first question is about legal authority: how much of the appropriation was released, committed and paid? The budget registries answer it. A registry is a list with a running balance. It is not a double-entry book. The budget unit keeps it. The second question is about financial position: what does the agency own and owe, and what did its operations cost? The accounting books answer it. They use double entry and the accrual basis. The Manual defines the accrual basis as a basis under which "transactions and other events are recognized when they occur (and not only when cash or its equivalent is received or paid)" [GAM-V1 Ch.2 s.2] . The accounting unit keeps the books. The Manual states this as the design of the whole system: "The financial reporting system of the Philippine government consists of accounting system on accrual basis and budget reporting system on budget basis" [GAM-V1 Ch.2 s.8] . The two sets do not record the same events. An obligation is an event for the registries only. The worked example of the Manual shows no journal entry for the budget law, for the allotment and for the obligation [GAM-V1 Annex H] . A depreciation charge is an event for the books only. A payment is an event for both. Outside the agency, three more bodies write about the same money. The servicing bank records what it paid from the account of the agency. BTr keeps the books of the national government for cash and debt. BIR records the tax that the agency withheld. Section 4.3 places all these records side by side. A case where the two sets of the agency agree: the disbursements in the registry of one period equal the credits to the cash accounts in the books for the same period and the same fund. Both are posted from the same daily reports of checks and payment orders issued [GAM-V1 Ch.3 ss.16-17] . A case where they disagree, without any error: the agency has obligated a contract of 100, has received and accepted deliveries worth 60, and has paid 40. The registry shows obligations of 100 and disbursements of 40. The books show an asset or expense of 60, a payable of 20 and a cash payment of 40. A reader who compares "obligations" with "expenses" finds a difference of 40. This difference is the part that is not yet delivered. Terms. RAPAL is the Registry of Appropriations and Allotments. RAOD is the Registry of Allotments, Obligations and Disbursements, kept for each expense class. RBUD is the Registry of Budget, Utilization and Disbursements, for funds outside the budget law. RANCA is the Registry of Allotments and Notice of Cash Allocation, the record in which the accounting unit follows the cash authority. JEV is the Journal Entry Voucher, the form on which one accounting entry is written. BFARs are the Budget and Financial Accountability Reports. A fund cluster is a group of funds with its own books and reports ( chapter 15 ).

t: 4.4 What follows from these tables
x: One payment has three dates. The agency credits its cash account on the day of its daily report, which also contains payment orders "not yet delivered" to the bank [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.52] . The bank credits the payee one or two days after it receives the order. The Treasury records the amount when the bank has paid. A payment order issued on the last day of a month is therefore paid in the books of the agency, and not yet paid in the records of the bank and of the Treasury. None of the three records is wrong. The cash account of the agency for its NCA is not money. The chart of accounts says that the account Cash-MDS, Regular "is used to recognize in the agency books the NCA received for its operating requirements" [GAM-V3 Ch.3] . The Manual says about year-end adjustments of bank accounts that they do not apply to this account, "since there is no actual cash with the GSBs" [GAM-V1 Ch.19 s.56] . GSB means government servicing bank. The account measures a limit that the agency may still use. The money stays in the accounts of the Treasury until the bank has paid ( chapter 11 ). Each body has an account that corresponds to an account of another body. The agency credits Subsidy from National Government, and the Treasury debits Subsidy to NGAs. The agency debits Cash-Treasury/Agency Deposit when it remits a collection, and the Treasury credits the account of the same name. The Manual calls the entry in the books of the other body the "responding entry" [GAM-V1 Annex H] . This is why the Manual requires that the books of each agency are "reconciled with the records of cash transactions maintained by the BTr" [GAM-V1 Ch.2 s.8] . The two sides do not record at the same moment. The agency records the subsidy when it receives the NCA, and it reverses the unused part at the end of the period. The Treasury records the subsidy when the bank has paid. At the end of a year the two amounts therefore differ by the checks and payment orders that the agency has issued and the bank has not yet paid. This sentence is my inference from the entries. The Manual does not state it in these words. One paper can produce entries in three sets of books without any movement of money. The Tax Remittance Advice is the example: the agency, BIR and the Treasury each make an entry from it [GAM-V1 Ch.5 s.38] .

t: Diagram 08a  The records inside one agency: which unit keeps which record, from which document, and which report is built from it
x: Code file: ../diagrams/mermaid/08a_accounting_records_flow.mmd . Rendered image: ../rendered/08a_accounting_records_flow.png . Question: inside one national agency, which unit keeps which record, from which document it is written, which unit passes its record to which other unit, and from which records are the reports built? Idea: four units of one agency write about the same money. The BUDGET UNIT keeps registries: lists with running balances that follow legal authority (appropriation, allotment, obligation, disbursement). The ACCOUNTING UNIT keeps the books: double entry on the accrual basis (assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses). The CASH UNIT keeps the records of receipts, checks and payment orders, and it reports to accounting every day. The PROPERTY UNIT keeps the cards of the items in stock and in use. The budget reports come from the registries. The financial statements come from the books. One statement, the comparison of budget and actual amounts, needs both. How to read it: top row (grey) = source documents. Blue frame = budget unit. Green frame = accounting unit. White frames = cash unit and property unit. Yellow = reports. A solid arrow = this document or record is the source of the next record. A dotted arrow = the two records are compared with each other. Numbers in brackets: "App." is the number of the form in Volume II of the Manual [GAM-V2] . Sources: the list of journals, ledgers and registries [GAM-V1 Ch.2 s.12] . Registries of the budget unit and the rule that a balance is extracted at every entry [GAM-V1 Ch.3 ss.5-12] . Part C of the obligation request as the subsidiary record of one obligation [GAM-V1 Ch.3 s.12] [GAM-V2 App.11] . The budget unit posts payments from the reports that accounting sends [GAM-V1 Ch.3 ss.16-17] . Registry of the NCA and index of payments [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] [GAM-V2 App.30, App.38] . Daily reports of the cash unit [GAM-V1 Ch.5 s.39, Ch.6 s.52, s.56] . Documents that are posted to the journals [GAM-V1 Ch.19 s.59] . Ledger cards of accounting and cards of the property unit, and their reconciliation [GAM-V1 Ch.8 s.9, Ch.10 s.42] . The six statements [GAM-V1 Ch.2 s.11] . The statement of comparison is prepared by the budget unit and verified by accounting [GAM-V1 Ch.3 ss.25-30] . The present set of budget reports and their route through URS [JC2019-1] . t: Diagram 08e  One event, several records: what each unit and each body writes for the same purchase (national agency, payment order, tax withheld)
x: Code file: ../diagrams/mermaid/08e_one_event_several_records.mmd . Rendered image: ../rendered/08e_one_event_several_records.png . Question: for each event of one purchase, which unit of the agency and which other body writes a record, what does each record say, and where does one body record nothing although another body has recorded the event? Idea: no single record contains the whole transaction. Five units or bodies write about the same money, each in its own record and on its own date. An obligation exists only in the registries of the budget unit. The first journal entry of the purchase itself is made when the delivery is accepted. The Treasury records the spending of the agency only when the bank has paid. A cell with the words "No record" is therefore information: it shows which body cannot see the event from its own records. How to read it: each row is one event, in the order of time. Each column is one keeper of records. Column 1 = the event. Column 2 (blue) = budget unit of the agency: registries, no double entry. Column 3 (green) = accounting unit of the agency: books with double entry. Column 4 (white) = cash unit and property unit of the agency. Column 5 (orange) = the servicing bank. Column 6 (yellow) = books of the national government kept by BTr. Column 7 (violet) = books of BIR. Grey with a dashed border = this keeper writes nothing at this event. The diagram has no arrows: the cells of one row are records of the same event, and they are not steps that follow one another. When the records agree: at the end of a month the cash account of the agency for its NCA equals the balance of the NCA in the bank statement, after the items in transit are listed. The monthly bank reconciliation statement shows this [GAM-V1 Ch.21] . When they disagree without an error: a payment order is issued on the last day of the month. The agency has credited its cash account (row 5). The bank and the Treasury have recorded nothing yet (row 6). The three records differ by this amount until the bank pays. t: 09. Audit and oversight
x: Part of the Philippine PFM Atlas. Facts as of 8 October 2026. The codes in the column "Basis" are explained in Reference F . "GK" means general knowledge that I did not open in a source during this work.

t: 1. The question this process answers
x: After public money is spent, who examines whether it was spent lawfully and well, and what happens when the answer is no?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
x: Every earlier step of the process is performed by the body that spends. Audit is the first examination by a body that does not spend and does not answer to the spender. In the Philippines this body is the Commission on Audit (COA) , which the Constitution makes independent and to which it gives the power to examine, audit and settle all accounts of the government [CONST IX-D.2] . Two features define the Philippine arrangement. First, the audit comes after payment . COA lifted its examination before payment (pre-audit) in 2011. It may restore pre-audit where the internal control of an agency is inadequate [COA2011-002] . The responsibility before payment therefore belongs to the management of the agency. Second, a finding on one transaction can become a personal liability . The Auditing Code says: "Expenditures of government funds or uses of government property in violation of law or regulations shall be a personal liability of the official or employee found to be directly responsible therefor" [PD1445 s.103] . The auditor can issue a notice that names the officers responsible and requires them to return the money. This is stronger than a recommendation in a report. The Code also fixes who answers first. "The head of any agency of the government is immediately and primarily responsible for all government funds and property pertaining to his agency" [PD1445 s.102] . An officer who holds funds or property is accountable for them and must be bonded [PD1445 s.101] . An order of a superior does not free this officer, unless the officer gave written notice beforehand that the order was illegal. In that case the superior is liable first [PD1445 s.106] . A case where the arrangement works: the auditor finds that a payment lacks a required document, suspends the amount, and the agency supplies the document. The suspension is lifted. A case where it fails: the auditor finds a pattern of weak spending in the yearly report and recommends changes, and no body with power over the agency acts on the report. The 2025 PEFA assessment found no formal scrutiny by the legislature of the audit reports on the annual financial reports (indicator 31, score D) [PEFA2025] . Terms. t: 1. The question this process answers
x: Which kinds of money does the national government receive, how does each kind reach the Treasury, and may the office that collects the money also spend it?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
x: The office that collects money is normally not the office that may spend it. A tax office collects taxes but its own budget comes from an appropriation like that of any other agency. All collections go to one place, the Treasury, and from there they are spent only through appropriations. This rule is what makes the budget complete: if agencies could spend what they collect, part of public money would never be examined by Congress. The law states the rule in three parts. Income of agencies is deposited in the National Treasury and credited to the General Fund unless a law provides otherwise [PD1445 s.65] . Every payment is acknowledged immediately: "No payment of any nature shall be received by a collecting officer without immediately issuing an official receipt in acknowledgment thereof" [PD1445 s.68] . Collecting officers "shall remit or deposit intact the full amounts" that they collect, and the treasury of the agency deposits them with the government depository "not later than the following banking day" [PD1445 s.69] . The accounting manual adds that no temporary receipt may be used for public funds, and that official receipts are numbered in advance and issued in the strict order of their numbers [GAM-V1 Ch.2 s.4] . The exceptions are all made by law, and each has its own kind of fund. A law earmarks a receipt for a purpose. The money is in the Treasury but in a special account in the General Fund , and may be spent only for that purpose. A law lets an agency keep and use its income. This is retained income or a revolving fund . It stays in a bank account of the agency, outside the yearly appropriation. The money is not the government's own: it is held for a purpose or for another party. These are trust receipts . A case where the rule works: a taxpayer pays through a bank, the bank remits to the Treasury on the same or the next day, and the cash is available for all payments of the government. The 2025 PEFA assessment found that BIR and BOC transfer their collections daily into the Treasury Single Account (indicator 20.2, score A) [PEFA2025] . A case where it fails: an agency keeps income in its own account under a special law, and this money is reported only in periodic reports. The Roadmap plans to include such off-budget accounts in BTMS or URS [SFA6] . Terms. An authorized agent bank is a bank that may receive tax payments. An authorized government depository bank is a bank that may receive the collections of agencies. The General Fund is the fund for all money that no law places elsewhere.

A tax that is assessed and not yet paid is in general not an asset in the books. The stock of revenue arrears that an assessment reports (section 11) therefore comes from the records of the tax offices and not from the accounts. Tax revenue is recorded at the gross amount. t: 11. Treasury: cash, the Treasury Single Account, borrowing and debt
p: 11. Treasury: cash, the Treasury Single Account, borrowing and debt
x: Part of the Philippine PFM Atlas. Facts as of 8 October 2026. The codes in the column "Basis" are explained in Reference F . "GK" means general knowledge that I did not open in a source during this work.

t: 1. The question this process answers
p: 11. Treasury: cash, the Treasury Single Account, borrowing and debt
x: Where is the cash of the national government held, who decides how much may be paid in a period, and how is the gap between receipts and payments financed?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
p: 11. Treasury: cash, the Treasury Single Account, borrowing and debt
x: The budget fixes how much may be spent in a year. It does not fix when the cash arrives. Tax collections are uneven during the year, and payments become due on their own dates. One office must therefore hold all the cash as one balance, forecast its movement, and borrow or invest so that money is there on the day a payment is due. This office is the Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) . Three arrangements make this possible. One balance. The Treasury Single Account (TSA) is, in the words of BTr, "a unified structure of government bank accounts" [BTR-SITE] . It is not one account and it is not software. It is a rule about bank accounts: the cash of the government is consolidated at the central bank so that BTr can see and use it as one amount. Limits, not cash, for agencies. An agency does not hold cash for its regular budget. It holds a limit (the NCA) at a servicing bank. The bank pays, and BTr repays the bank. Cash therefore stays in the single balance until the moment of payment. The accounting manual states the same fact for the books of an agency: for its account of the NCA "there is no actual cash with the GSBs", the government servicing banks [GAM-V1 Ch.19 s.56] . A cash program. BTr forecasts cash for the next three months [BTR-SITE] . DBM issues NCAs within that forecast. When cash is not sufficient, BTr borrows. When there is more than needed, BTr places it. The Administrative Code requires this: an operational cash budget, "to ensure the availability of cash resources for priority development projects and to establish a sound basis for determining the level, type and timing of public borrowings" [EO292-B6 s.36] . One rule of law stands behind all three. National funds "shall not be withdrawn from the National Treasury except upon warrant or other instruments of withdrawal approved by the Minister (Secretary) of Finance as recommended by the Treasurer of the Philippines" [PD1445 s.84] . The temporary investment of cash that is not needed immediately is not a disbursement [PD1445 s.84] . A case where this works: collections arrive daily, the forecast is close to the actual amounts, and cash is available for all NCAs that were issued. The 2025 PEFA assessment rates cash forecasting with the highest score, A (indicator 21.2) [PEFA2025] . A case where it fails: money is held in accounts outside the single balance, for example agency accounts for retained income or accounts of foreign-funded projects. The government then borrows and pays interest while it holds idle cash elsewhere. The same assessment states that accounts of foreign-funded projects and trust accounts with a legal basis remain outside the single account (indicator 21.1, score C) [PEFA2025] . Terms. Modified Disbursement System (MDS) : the arrangement of sub-accounts at servicing banks through which agencies pay. Government securities : Treasury bills and bonds, which are promises of the government to pay. Debt service : payment of interest and repayment of principal. Financing : borrowing and repayment, which are not revenue and not expenditure.

Question: in which bank accounts is the cash of the national government held, and which accounts are outside the single account? Idea: the Treasury Single Account (TSA) is not one account and not software. BTr defines it as a unified structure of government bank accounts. The balances are consolidated at the central bank so that BTr can see and use the cash as one amount. Agencies hold spending limits (NCA) at servicing banks, not cash. How to read it: thick arrows = cash. Grey boxes with a dashed border = accounts that are not part of the single account. Sources: definition and legal basis of the TSA (EO 55 of 2011, EO 338 of 1996, EO 431 of 2005), eTRAMS for collections reported by BIR, BOC and agencies [BTR-SITE] . TSA at BSP [ROADMAP2024] . MDS sub-accounts (regular, special accounts, trust, foreign-assisted projects) at LBP, DBP and PVB [NBC599] . Daily replenishment of servicing banks, the MDS seed fund [PRIMER] [CL2013-16A] . Same-day deposit of collections with authorized government depository banks, investment of idle balances, Bond Sinking Fund [EO449] . Daily transfer of collections, some foreign-funded and trust accounts outside the TSA [PEFA2025] . Shares of local governments released directly by BTr through servicing banks [GAA2026-GP] . Releases to corporations through BTr [BSGC2026] . Revolving funds in authorized depository banks [GAA2026-GP] . t: 12. Personnel and payroll
x: Part of the Philippine PFM Atlas. Facts as of 8 October 2026. The codes in the column "Basis" are explained in Reference F . "GK" means general knowledge that I did not open in a source during this work.

t: 1. The question this process answers
x: Salaries are paid without procurement. What replaces the contract and the delivery, who controls the number of positions and the amount of pay, and to whom does each part of the gross pay go?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
x: In a purchase, three things limit the payment. A contract fixes what is owed, a bid fixes the price, and an acceptance report proves that the supplier performed ( chapters 06 and 07). Personnel spending has none of these three. Three other things replace them. The position replaces the contract. A salary may be paid only for a position that DBM has authorized and that a person holds by a valid appointment. The salary schedule replaces the bid. The pay of a position follows from its salary grade and step under the compensation rules. The agency and the employee do not negotiate it. A certificate on the payroll replaces the acceptance report. On the payroll an authorized official certifies: "Services duly rendered as stated" [GAM-V2 App.33] . The attendance record supports this certificate, but it is not always there before the payment. The accounting manual says: "Payrolls are prepared in advance and some agencies pay their employees through the banking system. All these are done before reports of attendance are submitted, making it impossible to know the exact amount to be paid in case there are absences without pay" [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.48] . An overpayment is then demanded back from the employee. Points 1 and 2 are general knowledge. Point 3 is from the Manual. The sources that I opened also confirm the central record that supports point 1: DBM keeps the list of positions of every agency in the Government Manpower Information System (GMIS), each agency updates its part every month, and DBM computes the personnel budget from the positions that are filled [GMIS] . Two rules of law show how the budget treats personnel in a different way. The budget law does not list the single positions: it "shall not contain any itemization of personal services", and the Secretary of Budget and Management prepares that list for the approval of the President [EO292-B6 s.23, s.21] . And when the President suspends the spending of an agency, the pay of permanent staff is the one item that the law excepts [EO292-B6 s.38] . Because the pay of one position is fixed, the total cost depends almost only on the number of filled positions. The main control of personnel spending is therefore the control of the list of positions, and not the check of each payment. This is my conclusion from the three points. A case where the process works: a position is in the list, it is filled, and the agency budget of the year already contains its salary. The allotment exists from the first day of the budget law, because personnel services of filled positions are released by the law itself without a release document [NBC599] . The payroll of each period is then a routine payment. A case where it fails: an agency fills a vacant position in the middle of the year. The agency budget contains no money for it, because the budget was computed from the positions that were filled when the budget was prepared. The money is in a central fund, the Miscellaneous Personnel Benefits Fund, and it is released by a SARO [GMIS] [NBC599] . A second process, the request for this release, must therefore proceed at the same time as the payroll (inference from the two sources). A second case where it fails: the agency does not update its list in GMIS. The personnel budget of the next year is then computed from a wrong number of filled positions (inference from the rule that the budget follows the filled positions). Terms. A plantilla is the list of the authorized positions of an agency, with the person who holds each one. PSIPOP (Personal Services Itemization and Plantilla of Personnel) is the form of this list that is kept in GMIS . The Miscellaneous Personnel Benefits Fund and the Pension and Gratuity Fund are central funds in the budget law, outside the budgets of the agencies. Retirement and life insurance premiums are the share that the government pays as employer for the insurance of its employees (GK for this description). An Advice for use of PS Allotment (APSA) is the document by which available personnel allotment is used for a shortage in one personnel benefit. A Tax Remittance Advice records tax withheld by an agency as paid to BIR without a movement of cash.

t: 1. The question this process answers
x: After a supplier is paid, the budget records of that purchase end. In which records does the purchased item continue, who is responsible for it, and how does the government know what it owns?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
x: The budget follows money for one year. A building, a vehicle or a computer exists for many years. Two other kinds of record follow the item after the payment. The property record says where the item is and which officer is responsible for it. The accounting record says what the item cost and how much of that cost is not yet charged as an expense. The accounting manual prescribes both records for the same asset, in two different units: the ledger card in the accounting unit and the property card in the property unit. It requires that the two are reconciled [GAM-V1 Ch.10 s.42] . The reason is that the unit which holds the goods must not keep the only record of them. A physical count compares both records with the items that really exist. Without the count, the two records can agree with each other and still be wrong. Not every item is recorded in this full way. An item with a unit cost of PHP 50,000 or more is recorded as property, plant and equipment : an asset whose cost is distributed over the years of its use. An item below that amount is semi-expendable property : it is recorded as inventory when it is received and as an expense when it is issued to its user, and the item is still issued to a named officer and tracked [GAM-V1 Ch.8 s.10] [COA2022-004] . The amount of PHP 50,000 is from a circular of COA of 2022. The Manual of 2015 still prints the earlier amount of PHP 15,000 [GAM-V1 Ch.10 s.3] . The Manual gives five conditions for recording an item as property, plant and equipment: future benefit or service is probable, the cost can be measured, "beneficial ownership and control clearly rest with the government", the asset is used for the objectives of the government, and the threshold is met [GAM-V1 Ch.10 s.3] . The threshold applies to each item, and items that work together as one network count as one asset [GAM-V1 Ch.10 s.4] . A case where the process works: a vehicle is accepted, recorded as an asset in the books and in the property records, issued to a named officer, found at each yearly count, and removed from both records when it is sold. A case where it fails: the vehicle is paid and recorded in the accounting books, but the property record is not updated when the vehicle moves to another office. At the next count the books show an asset that the counting team cannot find in the place stated. The 2025 PEFA assessment rates the monitoring of non-financial assets C: the national registry is not yet in full use and does not record the age of assets [PEFA2025] . Terms. The capitalization threshold is the amount from which an item is recorded as an asset. Depreciation is the yearly charge that distributes the cost of an asset over its useful life. An Inventory Custodian Slip is the document by which semi-expendable property is issued to a user. An accountable officer is an officer who holds government money or property and is responsible for it.

t: A building or a road that is built under a contract
x: The cost of a work under construction is collected in the account Construction in Progress, on a ledger card that the accounting unit keeps for each project. The card names the project, the contract period, the contractor with its tax number, and the project cost, and it lists each voucher and journal entry [GAM-V2 App.77] . When the completed work is delivered and accepted, the cost moves to the asset account, for example Buildings [GAM-V1 Ch.10 s.8] . Chapter 07, section 7.2 , follows the payments of such a contract. Two rules on cost. Interest on a loan of the national government is an expense in the books of BTr and is not added to the cost of the asset in the books of the agency [GAM-V1 Ch.10 s.8] . An asset that a private operator builds under a concession is recorded by the government body that granted the concession, together with a liability of the same amount, when that body controls the services and the remaining interest in the asset [GAM-V1 Ch.14 s.3, s.5] . Chapter 19 describes such contracts.

t: Supplies
x: Supplies have two records in the same way: a supplies ledger card in the accounting unit, with quantities and cost, and a stock card in the property unit, with quantities only. They are counted every six months. An issue to a user is made on a requisition and issue slip, and the accounting unit charges the expense from a monthly report of the supplies issued [GAM-V1 Ch.8 s.9, s.13, s.16, Annex H] [GAM-V2 App.57, App.58, App.63] .

t: 14. Local governments
x: Part of the Philippine PFM Atlas. Facts as of 8 October 2026. The codes in the column "Basis" are explained in Reference F . "GK" means general knowledge that I did not open in a source during this work.

t: 1. The question this process answers
x: A local government has its own budget, separate from the budget law of the national government. Where does its money come from, who decides and who checks its budget, and at which points does it meet the national system?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
x: A local government unit (a province, a city, a municipality or a barangay) is a separate government. It has its own treasury, its own budget, its own legislature and its own accounts. Its yearly cycle repeats the national cycle on a smaller scale. The local chief executive (the governor or the mayor) corresponds to the President. The sanggunian (the local legislature) corresponds to Congress. Three things differ from the national cycle. A large part of the income is a share of national taxes, and it arrives without a decision each year. The share is 40 percent of the national taxes collected in the third fiscal year before the current one [LGC s.284] [MANDANAS] . The law appropriates it automatically [MANDANAS] [ALGU2026] , and the national government may not withhold it [LGC s.286] [CONST X.6] . National law fixes parts of the local budget. It sets minimum amounts for some purposes and maximum amounts for others [LGC s.287, s.324, s.325] . A higher authority reviews the budget after it is enacted. DBM reviews the appropriation ordinances of provinces, of highly urbanized cities, of independent component cities and of the municipalities in Metro Manila. The provincial sanggunian reviews those of component cities and municipalities [LGC s.326, s.327] . The national budget has no review of this kind. A case where the cycle works: the governor submits the executive budget by 16 October, the sanggunian enacts the ordinance before the year ends, and the reviewing authority finds it inside the legal limits or takes no action within 90 days. The ordinance is then in full force [LGC s.318, s.319, s.327] . A case where it fails: the sanggunian does not enact the ordinance before the fiscal year starts. It must stay in session and may consider no other business. If 90 days pass from the start of the fiscal year, the ordinance of the previous year is deemed reenacted, and only for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses [LGC s.323] . New projects cannot start. A second case where it fails: the review finds that items exceed a legal limit. The reviewing authority declares the ordinance inoperative in whole or in part, and the treasurer may make no further payment from the affected items [LGC s.327] . Terms. The National Tax Allotment (NTA) is the share of local governments in national taxes. Its older name is Internal Revenue Allotment. The local finance committee is the group of three local officers that estimates income and recommends the spending ceilings. An appropriation ordinance is the local law that authorizes the budget. BLGF is the Bureau of Local Government Finance of DOF. eSRE is the electronic Statement of Receipts and Expenditures, the reporting system of local treasurers.

t: The certifications before a payment
x: No money may be disbursed unless three officers have acted: the local budget officer certifies that an appropriation exists, the local accountant obligates it, and the local treasurer certifies that funds are available. The head of the department or office that controls the fund certifies and approves the voucher or payroll as to validity, propriety and legality. The local chief executive must also approve the voucher. This last approval is not required for regularly recurring administrative expenses, for example payrolls of regular employees, charges for light, water and telephone, and remittances to government creditor agencies. For a special or trust fund, the administrator of the fund approves [LGC s.344] .

t: 1. The question this process answers
p: 15. Government corporations, fund transfers, other spending paths, and fund clusters
x: Chapters 05 to 07 follow one purchase by one national agency. Which other routes does public money take, who approves the budget of a government corporation, when does a transfer to another body count as spent, and how does one agency separate different kinds of money?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
p: 15. Government corporations, fund transfers, other spending paths, and fund clusters
x: The main route is: an agency receives an allotment, procures, accepts a delivery and pays. Four things do not fit this route, and each has its own rule. A government corporation is not an agency in the budget law. It is a separate legal person with its own income. Its yearly budget is the Corporate Operating Budget , which its governing board approves and DBM reviews [COB] . The Administrative Code has the rule: the internal operating budgets of these corporations "shall be approved by their respective governing boards", and they pass through the budget process of the national government "in cases where national government budgetary support is needed" [EO292-B6 s.19] . Only the money that the national government gives to it (a subsidy, or equity, which is a capital investment) passes through the budget law and the Treasury [BSGC2026] . A fund transfer moves cash, but it does not move the responsibility. When an agency gives money to another agency, a corporation or a local government to implement a project, the source agency may not treat the money as disbursed until the receiver has used it for works, goods or services that were completed, inspected and accepted [NBC599 s.3.4] . Several kinds of spending omit steps of the main route. Salaries have no procurement. The share of local governments has no voucher of an agency. Interest on debt has no yearly vote on the amount. Diagram 15c shows eight such paths. One agency holds several kinds of money. Money from the budget law, money from loans, income that the agency may keep, and money held for others must be recorded and reported separately. Each group is a fund cluster with its own books [JC2017-1] [JC2019-1] . The accounting manual requires "fund cluster accounting" as one of its basic principles, and each agency keeps a complete set of books for each cluster [GAM-V1 Ch.2 s.6, s.8] . A case where the transfer rule works: in March an agency transfers 100 to a second agency for a project. The second agency procures, accepts the work in October, pays 90, reports this and returns 10. The first agency then reports a disbursement of 90. A case where it fails: the second agency does not report. The books of the first agency show a receivable for years. The cash left the Treasury in March, and no record of the first agency shows what was bought. The 2025 PEFA assessment found that a part of the advances, in particular those given to government corporations, was not liquidated at the end of 2023 [PEFA2025] . Terms. A GOCC is a government-owned or controlled corporation. A subsidy is money for the operations or programs of the corporation (GK for this short definition). Equity is a capital investment of the national government in the corporation, and may not be used for salaries [BSGC2026] . Liquidation means that the receiver of an advance or transfer reports, with documents, how the money was used. Off-budget means not appropriated each year in the budget law.

t: 5.1 Money for disasters
p: 15. Government corporations, fund transfers, other spending paths, and fund clusters
x: After a disaster, money is needed within days, and the main route takes months. Diagram 15e answers the question: which money is already available, who must approve the rest, and which records show the use? The idea: speed is obtained in three ways, and none of them removes the normal controls of appropriation, obligation, voucher and audit. Way Content Who decides Basis Quick Response Fund of an agency An amount kept ready inside the budget of twelve agencies and corporations (the rules call it a standby fund), among them the social welfare, education, public works, agriculture and health departments and the Office of Civil Defense. PHP 10.69 billion in FY 2026. The agency uses it immediately The agency. When the balance decreases to 50 percent, it asks DBM to replenish the fund GAA2026-NDRRMF , DBM-QRF National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund PHP 39.82 billion in the FY 2026 budget law, with no project named in advance. Four purposes: relief and rehabilitation services (11.03 billion), repair and reconstruction (12.47 billion), the People's Survival Fund (1.00 billion), and assistance to local governments for rehabilitation and reconstruction (15.33 billion). It covers events of the current year and of the two years before The President approves each use, with the recommendation of the national disaster council. DBM then issues a SARO GAA2026-NDRRMF Fund of each local government Not less than 5 percent of estimated revenue from regular sources, in every yearly budget. 30 percent of it is a Quick Response Fund. Amounts not spent go to a special trust fund for five years and then return to the general fund The local government. The condition for the use of the 30 percent, and who approves, are not verified RA10121 (read in two documents that quote the law and its rules) What the records show. DBM publishes the status of the national fund each month, with the number, date and amount of each SARO. By 31 May 2026 it had released PHP 5.92 billion, all in three SAROs to the social welfare department to replenish its Quick Response Fund. One of them is SARO-BMB-B-26-0000189 of 12 February 2026 for PHP 1,979,556,861 [NDRRMF-STATUS] . Implementing agencies report each quarter through URS and publish the reports on their websites [GAA2026-NDRRMF] . Procurement in an emergency: the Implementing Rules allow negotiated procurement when there is imminent danger to life or property during a calamity, or when vital services must be restored. Some documents of the supplier may then be submitted after the award, before payment [IRR12009 s.35.2] . On 14 August 2026 the GPPB approved guidelines for procurement in four stages: preparedness, action before an expected disaster, response and recovery. Emergency negotiated procurement applies "When time is of the essence arising from natural or man-made calamities", and also for action before a disaster once a state of imminent disaster is declared. The guidelines encourage framework agreements for goods that will be needed ( chapter 06, section 5 ), and they allow the steps of a procurement before the award to be done early. The entity must confirm that "there is a budget for the purpose", and the contract form has a line "Certified Funds Available" for the chief accountant. Payment stays "subject to existing budgeting, accounting and auditing rules and regulations". A performance security is at the option of the entity. The guidelines do not speak of the Quick Response Fund or of advance payment [GPPB2026-17] . I read them as a summary. They shorten the choice of the supplier. They do not change the controls of funds: the certificate of the accountant, the obligation and the voucher remain. A case where the design works: a typhoon damages schools. The education department repairs classrooms immediately from its Quick Response Fund, and asks for replenishment when half of it is used. A case where it fails: the damage is larger than these ready amounts, and the release from the national fund needs a recommendation and an approval. The time between the disaster and the SARO is then the time of these two steps. The sources that I read do not state how long they take.

t: 1. The question this chapter answers
x: Which information system holds which record today, which institution owns it, by which carrier does each record pass from one system or body to the next, and what is the planned Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS) meant to change? The inventory of all systems, with owner, user and recipient of each one, is in Reference B . Reference B also contains a register of every flow between two systems or bodies. For each flow the register says what passes, by which carrier, whether it is in use, which control compares both sides, and where I read it. This chapter explains how the systems relate to each other.

t: 2. The idea in plain words
x: Each institution built a system for its own part of the process. DBM has systems for budget proposals, positions, releases and reports. COA gives agencies systems for registries and books. BTr has systems for collections, cash and securities. BIR, BOC, the banks and DEPDev have their own. Each system serves the part of the process for which it was built. The difficulty lies between the systems. For most flows the sources describe a person who enters or uploads the content in the next system, or a paper copy. For few flows they describe a program that sends to another program, and for many they do not say how the content passes (section 6, and Reference B, section 4.4 ). The Roadmap names three gaps of this arrangement: the same report is prepared more than once, processing is manual, and the systems are not integrated [ROADMAP2024] . There are two ways to integrate. In the first, one large system replaces all the others. In the second, each institution keeps its system, one system holds the central records of budget execution, and the other systems exchange agreed records with it through interfaces. An interface (in the documents: API, application programming interface) is a defined way in which one program sends data to another and receives data from it. The Philippine plan is the second way. The Roadmap describes interfaces that connect the existing separate systems to a central core, and says that agencies keep their existing systems [ROADMAP2024] . Its action plan calls BTMS the "interoperable core" of the IFMIS [SFA6] . A case where this design works: system A and system B use the same code for the same budget line and the same number for the same document. A record made in A can then be found in B without the help of a person. A case where it fails: A and B use different codes, or give the same word different meanings. The interface then passes records that cannot be matched with each other. The action plan names this gap ("inconsistent classification codes across PFM systems") and plans three remedies: a review of UACS, one PFM data model, and a metadata registry, which is a list of the agreed definition of every data field [SFA6] . Terms. IFMIS : the Integrated Financial Management Information System that Executive Order No. 29 of 2023 tells all national government entities to adopt. BTMS : the Budget and Treasury Management System of DBM. Core : the system that holds the central records and to which the others connect. Rollout : the introduction of a system in one group of agencies after another.

t: 6. What passes between systems and bodies today, and by which carrier
x: Diagrams 16b (spending side) and 16g (revenue and treasury side) show the systems inside their owner institutions, with what passes between them. Diagram 08a shows what passes between the units of one agency. The tables below list the same flows. They are produced from the register in Reference B, section 4 , which has two more columns for each flow: the control that compares both sides, and the basis. One word for each flow, such as "Electronic", would mix three different questions. The tables answer them one by one. Kind : what passes. Data, a document, an authority (a document that gives a right or sets a limit), or money. Carrier : how it passes. "System to system" means that one program sends to another and no person copies the content. "Entry by the sender" means that a person of the sending body enters or uploads the content in a system of the receiver. "Entry in own system" means that staff enter it in a record or system of their own body. "Paper" means signed paper copies. "Electronic, kind not stated" means that a source describes an electronic channel and does not say of which kind. Stage of use : whether a source describes the flow as existing today, as existing for a part of the agencies, as required or described without a confirmation of use, or as planned. "Not stated" never means "absent". It means that the sources that I read do not say. A case where the difference matters: an agency sends its budget forms to DBM through OSBPS. A source describes this as an online submission [NBM156] . That is an electronic flow, and it is also a second entry by a person: the staff of the agency type or upload the figures that they hold in their own files. The carrier "Entry by the sender" says both things. The one word "Electronic" hid the second.

t: 17. UACS and the identifiers of records
p: 17. UACS and the identifiers of records
x: Part of the Philippine PFM Atlas. Facts as of 8 October 2026. The codes in the column "Basis" are explained in Reference F . "GK" means general knowledge that I did not open in a source during this work.

t: 1. The question this chapter answers
p: 17. UACS and the identifiers of records
x: Is the Unified Accounts Code Structure (UACS) the key that connects all PFM records? What does a UACS code say about an amount, on which records does it appear, and which other numbers are needed to follow one transaction from the budget to the audit?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
p: 17. UACS and the identifiers of records
x: Two different questions can be asked about a record of public money. The first question is: to which group does this amount belong? Which fund, which office, which program, which kind of expense? A classification answers it. A classification is a set of codes, and many records have the same code. The second question is: which single record is this, and from which earlier record does it come? An identifier answers it. An identifier is a number that only one record has, for example the number of one obligation request. UACS is a classification. It is the common classification of the budget, of the accounting books and of the reports of the national government [JC2017-1] . It is not an identifier. A case where UACS is enough: "How much was allotted, obligated and paid under this program of this agency for capital outlays in 2026?" All records with the same code are summed. Report FAR 1 does this [JC2019-1] . A case where UACS is not enough: one budget line funds two contracts, A and B. Every record of A and every record of B has the same UACS code. The question which payments belong to contract B, and whether the work of B was accepted before each payment, cannot be answered from the code. The answer needs the chain of document numbers: the number of the obligation request, of the voucher and of the payment order [GAM-V2 App.11, App.32, App.42] . Diagram 17d shows this case with invented numbers. The answer to the hypothesis "UACS is the key" therefore has two parts. A common classification is one of two ways to make totals comparable. The totals of two systems can be compared when both use the same classification, or when a documented table translates the codes of one into the codes of the other. The law chose the first way: "A common terminology and classification shall be used consistently throughout the budget, the accounts and the financial reports" [PD1445 s.115] . UACS is the classification that the present rules prescribe for this purpose [JC2017-1] . The second way exists in the rules too: when COA replaced the chart of accounts, it issued rules for the conversion from the old chart to the new one [GAM-V3 Ch.1] . A classification is not sufficient. To follow one transaction, each record must also contain its own number and the number of the record from which it comes. Terms. A segment is one of the five parts of a UACS code. An element is a part of a segment. PAP means program, activity or project. The object code says what is bought or paid. A responsibility center is a part of an agency whose head is responsible for a set of activities. In a database, a key is a field by which two records are joined: the primary key is the record's own number, and a foreign key is the number of another record that it quotes.

t: 4. Structure of the code
p: 17. UACS and the identifiers of records
x: Diagram 17a shows the structure. A full code has 54 digits in five segments. Segment Digits Elements, with the digits of each Question that it answers Basis 1. Funding source 8 Fund cluster 2, financing source 1, authorization 2, fund category 3 Which money is it? JC2017-1 2. Organization 12 Department 2, agency 3, operating unit class 2, lower-level operating unit 5 Which office is responsible? JC2017-1 3. Location 9 Region 2, province 2, city or municipality 2, barangay 3 For which area? JC2017-1 4. Program, activity, project 15 Cost structure 1, organizational outcome 1, program 2, sub-program 2, identifier 1, activity or project 5, reserved 3 For what purpose? JC2017-1 5. Object 10 Account code of the Revised Chart of Accounts 8, sub-object 2 What is bought or paid? JC2017-1 , GAM-V3 Ch.2 Details. Fund cluster (first two digits of segment 1): the seven groups 01 to 07 of chapter 15 [JC2017-1] . Cost structure (first digit of segment 4): 1 general administration and support, 2 support to operations, 3 operations, 4 special purpose funds [JC2017-1] . Identifier in segment 4: 1 activity, 2 locally funded project, 3 foreign-assisted project [JC2017-1] . Object code : the chart of accounts lists each account with a code of eight digits, a sub-object code of two digits, and the object code, which is the first followed by the second. Example of the chart: the account Cash-Collecting Officers has the account code 10101010 and the object code 1010101000. The first digit of an account code says what the account is: 1 an asset, 2 a liability, 3 equity, 4 revenue, 5 an expense [GAM-V3 Ch.2] . The object code of the budget and the account code of the books are therefore one code by construction. This is the point where the budget classification and the accounting books meet. Responsibility center code : the Manual defines it as the organization code of UACS, 12 digits, followed by 3 digits for the major office inside the agency [GAM-V1 Ch.4 s.7] . Several forms carry it (section 5). Not all digits on every document. The website of UACS says that not all 54 digits are used on each document [UACS-FAQ] . Removed in 2017. Codes for sector and for function are no longer part of the code. DBM keeps them as tags in a separate database [JC2017-1] .

t: A contradiction between two sources on the location segment
