t: 1. The question this process answers
x: The budget law gives each program an amount in pesos and also a target in units, for example a number of classrooms. Who records whether the target was reached, who checks that record, and who uses it? And what is the difference between monitoring, performance review, evaluation and audit?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
x: Money has a line of records: appropriation, allotment, obligation, payment. Performance has a second line of records, parallel to the first. The target is written in the budget, with the appropriation. The plan divides the target among the quarters of the year. The quarterly report states what the agency delivered. The yearly review by DBM compares the reports with the targets. The two lines have no arithmetic connection. A report of money says how much was committed or paid. A report of performance says how many units were delivered. The only connection is that both are organized by program. Diagram 08c shows this as measure E beside the four measures of money. Four different examinations use these records. Each one answers a different question. Monitoring asks whether the work is on schedule. Performance review asks whether the targets were reached. Evaluation asks whether the program caused the result that was intended. Audit asks whether the money was spent lawfully and whether the accounts are correct. Diagram 18b shows the four together. A case where the reported result is reliable: the target is a count of things that the agency itself delivers, for example kilometres of road completed. The count can be checked against contracts and acceptance reports, which are records of the money line. A case where it is not: the target is a condition that depends on many actors, for example the share of pupils who complete school. The agency can report the figure, but the report does not show whether its spending caused the figure. A program can therefore reach every target and still have no effect, or have an effect that the targets do not show. Only an evaluation can separate the two. Terms. An output is what the agency delivers (a classroom, a training course). An outcome is the change that the output is meant to produce (pupils who learn, trained persons who find work). An indicator is a measure with a unit, for which a target is set for the year. The program classification (Program Expenditure Classification, PREXC) is the arrangement of the budget of each agency by programs, each with indicators.

t: 3. Authorities and their roles
x: The law gave this task to the budget department long before the present reports. The Administrative Code of 1987 says: "The President, through the Secretary shall evaluate on a continuing basis the quantitative and qualitative measures of agency performance as reflected in the units of work measurement and other indicators of agency performance, including the standard and actual costs per unit of work" [EO292-B6 s.51] . The same chapter requires standard costs for each unit of work, a continuing review of the programs of each agency, and a report of each head of agency every six months on "both work and financial results" [EO292-B6 s.54, s.55, s.56] . A failure to submit the required reports stops the salary of the officials responsible [EO292-B6 s.57] . The present reports BED 2 and BAR 1 are the form in which these duties are performed today. Question: the budget law contains targets in units (for example classrooms built), not only amounts in pesos. Where is a target written, who reports the result, who checks the report, and who uses it? Idea: performance information has its own line of records, parallel to the line of money. t: 1. The question this process answers
p: 19. Fiscal risks, public-private partnerships and contingent liabilities
x: The budget law lists the spending that is decided for one year. Which payments may become necessary although no budget line of today names them, who monitors each source of such payments, and from which authority would they be paid?

t: 2. The idea in plain words
p: 19. Fiscal risks, public-private partnerships and contingent liabilities
x: A fiscal risk is an event that would make revenue, spending or debt differ from the plan. Some risks are general, for example slower growth of the economy. Others come from promises that the government has already made. A contingent liability is such a promise: the government will pay IF a stated event occurs. Example: the national government guarantees a loan of a government corporation. If the corporation repays the loan, the government pays nothing. If the corporation cannot repay, the government must pay the lender. The difficulty for the budget process is the date. On the day of the promise no money leaves the Treasury, so no appropriation, no obligation and no payment is recorded. The promise does not appear in any record of chapters 05 to 08. It appears only in two places: in a statement of risks, and later, if the event occurs, as a payment for which an authority must then exist. The accounting rules say the same for the books. The Manual defines a contingent liability as "A possible obligation that arises from past events, and whose existence will be confirmed only by the occurrence or non-occurrence of one or more uncertain future events not wholly within the control of the entity", or a present obligation for which a payment is not probable or cannot be measured [GAM-V1 Ch.18 s.2] . Its rule is: "An entity shall not recognize a contingent liability. However, it is disclosed unless the possibility of an outflow of resources" is remote [GAM-V1 Ch.18 s.3] . A guarantee that is not yet called is therefore named in the notes to the financial statements and is not a liability in the statement of financial position. It becomes a recorded liability, called a provision, when a payment is probable and the amount can be estimated [GAM-V1 Ch.18 s.3] . The law has one authority ready for the day on which a guarantee is called: "national government guarantees of obligations which are drawn upon" are among the automatic appropriations [EO292-B6 s.26] . A public-private partnership (PPP) produces both kinds of future payment. A private firm pays for the construction of a road or a hospital and operates it. The government pays later in instalments, or promises support under stated conditions. The decision is made once, at the signing of the contract, and it binds the budgets of many later years. For such a contract the Manual has a rule that differs from the rule for a guarantee. The government body that grants the concession records the asset that the private operator builds, when it "controls or regulates what services the operator must provide with the asset, to whom it must provide them, and at what price" and controls the remaining interest in the asset at the end of the term [GAM-V1 Ch.14 s.3] . With the asset it records a liability of the same amount: a financial liability when the government must pay the operator, or the grant of a right when the operator earns from the users [GAM-V1 Ch.14 s.5] . A partnership of this kind is therefore in the books from the start, and a guarantee is not. A case where the control works: before a partnership contract is signed, a body above the agency approves the project, and the Department of Finance clears each promise of the national government. The yearly payments are then included in each budget proposal, and a fund exists for the promises that become due. A case where it fails: a promise is given outside these procedures, for example a guarantee in the charter of a corporation or a letter of support, and nobody records it. It appears for the first time when the creditor asks for payment. The budget of that year has no line for it. Terms. An availability payment is a regular payment by the government to the private partner for keeping the facility available, whether or not the public uses it. A government undertaking is any contribution or support that the government gives to the private partner, for example a subsidy or a guarantee. Viability gap funding is a subsidy that makes a project financially possible for the private partner when the income from users is too low. Net lending is the amount that the national government lends to government corporations, less repayments.

Which possible payments are not decided, where could they come from, who monitors each source, and from which authority would a payment be made if the event occurs? Idea: a fiscal risk is an event that would change revenue, spending or debt compared with the plan. One group of risks are contingent liabilities: the government has promised to pay IF a stated event occurs (for example, if a corporation cannot repay a guaranteed loan). Such a promise costs nothing on the day it is made, so it does not appear as spending. It appears only in a risk statement, until the event occurs. How to read it: each row is one source of risk, in the order of the chapters of the Fiscal Risks Statement. Column 2 = the office that monitors it. Column 3 (grey) = the authority from which a payment would be made if the event occurs. Sources: the Fiscal Risks Statement is issued by the DBCC. Its chapters cover macroeconomic assumptions, fiscal performance, public debt, the financial sector, and "Other Contingent Central Government Obligations": government corporations, public-private partnerships and other contingent liabilities, local governments, natural disasters [FRS2023] . Members of the DBCC [DBCC-PAGE] [AO37] . Interest and net lending as automatic appropriations, budgetary support to corporations, the Contingent Fund and the disaster fund as items released by SARO [NBC599] . The PPP Risk Management Fund pays contingent liabilities from partnerships; the PPP Center manages it and the DBCC sets its target amount [RA11966 s.27] . Disaster funds, see 15e [GAA2026-NDRRMF] . BLGF certifies the borrowing capacity of local governments [DOF-LGULOAN] . Rows of the consolidated public sector position [BESF2026-A3] . In the accounts and in the law: a contingent liability is disclosed in the notes and is not recorded as a liability [GAM-V1 Ch.18 s.3] . A guarantee of the national government that is called is paid from an automatic appropriation, and corporations report their guaranteed obligations to DOF and DBM [EO292-B6 s.26, s.30] . An asset built by a private operator under a concession is recorded by the government body that granted it, with a liability of the same amount [GAM-V1 Ch.14 s.3, s.5] . General knowledge, not opened in a source here: that DOF and BTr decide on guarantees for the loans of corporations; that the Governance Commission for GOCCs monitors the performance of corporations; unprogrammed appropriations as a source of payment; the statement in row 5 that no national authority pays the debts of a local government by rule. The latest Fiscal Risks Statement that I could open is that of 2023, and its last chapter was cut in my copy. Not covered by the assessment pages I read: indicator 10 (fiscal risk reporting) of the 2025 assessment [PEFA2025] .

t: Diagram 19b  A national public-private partnership: approvals, promises of the government, and the two links to the budget (PlantUML)
p: 19. Fiscal risks, public-private partnerships and contingent liabilities
x: Code file: ../diagrams/plantuml/19b_ppp_project_swimlane.puml . Rendered image: ../rendered/19b_ppp_project_swimlane.png . Question: in a public-private partnership a private firm pays for the construction and the government pays later, or promises to pay if a stated event occurs. Which bodies approve such a project, and at which points does it enter the budget? Idea: a partnership moves payments into later years and adds promises that depend on events. The controls are therefore placed before the contract is signed: approval by a body above the agency when the cost is high or when money of the budget is promised, and clearance of each promise by the Department of Finance. After signing, two budget links remain: yearly payments that need an appropriation each year, and a fund for the promises that become due. How to read it: one column (lane) = one actor. A diamond = a decision. The notes on the right name the two points where the project enters the budget. Why PlantUML: the path crosses seven actors, and lanes show which actor decides at each step. Sources: all steps are from the Public-Private Partnership Code of 2023 [RA11966] : approval thresholds and exceptions (section 7), clearance by DOF of the draft contract when the national government gives an undertaking (section 8), unsolicited proposals and the right to match within 30 days (section 10), monitoring reports under oath and the yearly report of the PPP Center to Congress (section 16), PPP Center and PPP Governing Board (sections 24 and 25), Project Development and Monitoring Facility (section 26), PPP Risk Management Fund (section 27), audit and the accounting framework (section 31). Names: the Code names the "NEDA Board" and its Investment Coordination Committee (ICC). A law of 2025 replaced the NEDA Board by the Economy and Development Council [AO37] . The diagram uses the present name and adds the name of the Code. Not opened: the implementing rules of the Code. A press report of October 2025 says that the ICC review threshold for projects paid from the national budget was raised to PHP 5 billion and that the review now covers partnerships [ICC-NEWS] . I did not check how that threshold relates to the PHP 15 billion of the Code.

t: 1. Three roles around each system
p: Reference B. Inventory of information systems
x: For each system it is useful to separate three roles, because they are often held by three different institutions. The owner builds and controls the system. The user is the office that enters the data. The recipient is the office that receives or reads the data. Example: COA owns eNGAS, the accounting unit of each agency is the user, and COA auditors are among the recipients. A table that names only the owner hides who is responsible for the correctness of the data, and that is the user. Diagram 00c shows the systems by owner. Diagrams 16b and 16g show what passes between them, and diagram 08a shows what passes between the units of one agency. Section 4 of this file lists every one of these flows with its kind, its carrier, its stage of use, the control that compares both sides, and the evidence. Diagram 16a shows the systems by PFM function.

t: 4. Register of interfaces: every flow between two systems or bodies, with the evidence for it
p: Reference B. Inventory of information systems
x: A diagram of systems is quick to draw and difficult to verify, because an arrow between two boxes can mean very different things: a program that sends data to another program, a person who types the same data again, a paper that is carried, a movement of money, or a plan. One word for the state of an arrow cannot hold all of this. The register therefore answers five separate questions for each flow of diagrams 16b, 16g and 08a. Column Question Values Kind What passes? Data : figures or records. Document : a signed paper, or a copy or file of it. Authority : a document that gives a right or sets a limit, for example an allotment or a Notice of Cash Allocation. Money : money moves between two accounts or persons Carrier How does it pass? System to system : one program sends to another, and no person copies the content. Entry by the sender : a person of the sending body enters or uploads the content in a system of the receiving body. Download by the receiver : a person of the receiving body takes a file from a system of the sending body. Entry in own system : staff enter the content in a record or system of their own body. Electronic, kind not stated : a source describes an electronic channel and does not say which of the kinds above it is. Paper : signed paper copies are sent or carried. Bank transfer and Cash or check : for money. Public website : published for any person. Not stated : a source says that the content passes, and not how Stage of use Is it used today? In use . In use for part : only some agencies or banks use it. Described or required, use not verified : a rule or the owner describes it, and no source confirms the use. Planned . Not stated Check of both sides Which control compares what the sender recorded with what the receiver recorded? Free text. "None stated" means that I read no such control Basis Where did I read it? A source code of Reference F . "GK" means that the flow itself is from general knowledge. For such a row the carrier and the stage are "Not stated" Each row has a number that stays fixed, so that other files can cite it. A row that is added receives the next free number and stands in the table of its side. A row that is removed leaves its number unused. One rule of reading: "Not stated" never means "absent". It means that the sources that I read do not say. A flow with the carrier "Not stated" may be a file, a paper, a second entry by a person, or an interface between two programs. A case where the register is useful: a model assumes that an obligation recorded by an agency is known to DBM immediately. Row 15 shows that the obligation is entered by agency staff in a registry of the agency, and row 12 shows that DBM receives the figures through reports, which are quarterly for obligations. The assumption is wrong for every agency that is not on BTMS. A second case: a model assumes that the bank and the Treasury learn of a payment from a system. Rows 32 to 34 and row 19 show that the Manual of 2015 prescribes paper copies between the agency, the bank and the Treasury, and row 17 shows an electronic facility that only the agencies with accounts at one bank can use. A case where the register is not enough: the stage "In use" says that a source describes the flow as existing. It does not say that the flow works without error or delay, and it does not say what the receiving side does with the content. The last column names the control that could show this, where I read one.

t: 5. Status of BTMS in October 2026
p: Reference B. Inventory of information systems
x: Fact Basis BTMS was first adopted for budget execution by DBM Circular Letter No. 2019-4, and later revived CL2025-8 The present system was launched in May 2025. It processed about PHP 4.25 billion from its first transactions on 17 December 2025 to the end of that year INQ-BTMS DBM Circular Letter No. 2025-8 of 28 August 2025 makes BTMS the primary system for expenditure transactions of all national agencies with appropriations in the GAA, in a phased rollout. DBM issues the rollout schedule CL2025-8 DBM and BTr use the system. Five more pilot agencies prepare in 2026. Plan: 110 agencies in 2027 and 198 in 2028, total 315. The action plan of the Roadmap counts 2, then 115, then 198 INQ-BTMS , SFA6 A third source gives other dates and numbers. In a speech of 22 January 2026 the Secretary of Budget and Management said that BTMS was launched in 2024, was piloted with seven agencies in 2025, and would reach 155 national agencies in 2026. The atlas states the three sources and does not decide between them DBM-SPEECH26 Target share of the budget executed through BTMS: 50 percent, then 80 percent SFA6 A third-party audit and certification of BTMS is planned for 2026 and 2027 SFA6 Reports are submitted through URS or other electronic means until agencies migrate to BTMS GAA2026-GP Governance: PFM Committee, a Central Project Management Group, and the DBM project management office. Each agency forms a project implementation team, prepares a security access matrix and migrates its data CL2025-8 Interfaces (APIs) are foreseen with procurement, document management, electronic funds transfer and financial systems. Which interfaces are already in use: not verified CL2025-8

The present state of TradeNet, of the Customs Processing System and of the Real Property Information System. Whether certificates of the PNPKI are used to sign PFM documents. The network and record format of the DBM blockchain application. Press reports that quote the vendor name a public network and a token for each document. The DBM page does not state them.

t: Reference C. Documents, records and their identifiers
p: Reference C. Documents, records and their identifiers
x: Part of the Philippine PFM Atlas. Facts as of 8 October 2026. The codes in the column "Basis" are explained in Reference F . "GK" means general knowledge that I did not open in a source during this work. This file lists the documents of the process. For each one it says who issues it, what it does, and how it is identified. Section 11 adds, for 39 records, what each one proves and what it does not prove. Two kinds of identifier exist, and the difference matters for any attempt to connect records (see chapter 17 ). A document number identifies one document, for example one SARO or one voucher. A classification code (UACS) says to which class the amount belongs. Many documents have the same code. The forms of sections 5, 6 and 8 are read in Volume II of the Government Accounting Manual, which contains each form and its instructions [GAM-V2] . "App." is the number of the form there. The Manual is of 2015. Where a later rule changed a form or an amount, the row says so, as far as I checked.

t: 1. Why the rules are in layers
x: Philippine PFM has no single finance law. The rules are in five layers, and a lower layer may not contradict a higher one. The Constitution fixes who may do what: who proposes the budget, who may change it, who audits. Laws that stay in force for many years fix the general process: the Administrative Code, the Auditing Code, the Local Government Code, the procurement law. The General Appropriations Act of each year fixes the amounts, and its general and special provisions add rules for that year only. Executive orders of the President set policy inside the Executive, for example cash budgeting or the adoption of an integrated system. Circulars of DBM, COA, DOF, BTr and GPPB give the working detail: forms, deadlines, steps. A consequence for anyone who maps the process: many details (validity of appropriations, release documents, reports) are in layers 3 and 5 and change from year to year. Each chapter of this atlas therefore says for which fiscal year a rule was read.

x: Term Meaning Do not confuse with Accounts payable Amounts that the government owes for deliveries already accepted. The Manual calls them valid and legal obligations for which goods, services or projects were delivered, rendered or completed, and accepted. (07) An obligation, which exists from the contract on, before any delivery Accrual basis A way of accounting that records an expense when the goods or services are received, not when the cash is paid. The Government Accounting Manual uses it. (08) The budget reports, which count obligations and disbursements. The two give different amounts for the same year Advance payment A payment under a contract before the delivery. The law allows it only with the approval of the President. The procurement rules of 2025 name the cases, and in several of them they require a security, for example a bank guarantee. The advance is recovered from later payments. (07) A cash advance, which is given to an officer of the agency and not to a supplier Allotment An authorization by DBM that allows an agency to incur obligations up to an amount, for a purpose and a period. It contains no cash. (05) The appropriation, which is the law, and the Notice of Cash Allocation, which is the limit for payments Allotment class, also expense class One of four groups of spending: personnel services, maintenance and other operating expenses, financial expenses, capital outlays. (05) The object code of UACS, which is a finer class inside an allotment class Appropriation An authorization made by law to pay money from the Treasury for a stated purpose. (04) Money in an account. An appropriation is a permission Appropriation ordinance The budget law of a local government, enacted by its sanggunian. (14) The General Appropriations Act, which is national Augmentation Adding to an item of appropriation that is deficient, from savings in other items. Only five officials named in the Constitution may be authorized to do it, each for the own office. (05) A modification, which changes amounts inside one item and needs no savings Automatic appropriation An appropriation made by a standing law, so that Congress does not vote the amount each year. Examples: interest payments, the National Tax Allotment. (04) An automatic release. Several automatic appropriations still need a release document of DBM Availability payment A regular payment by the government to the private partner of a partnership for keeping a facility available, whether or not the public uses it. (19) A government undertaking. The Code treats the two as different things Bicameral conference A meeting of members of the House and the Senate that reconciles two versions of a bill. (04) Books of accounts The journals and ledgers that the accounting unit keeps by double entry, for each fund cluster. (08) The registries of the budget unit. Both record the same spending, at different moments Budget Call The yearly memorandum by which DBM tells agencies how to prepare their proposals. (03) The budget ceiling of an agency, which is one content of the Call Call-Off An order under a framework agreement. It is a purchase order, and a certificate of availability of funds is issued for each one. (06) The framework agreement itself, for which no certificate is issued Capital outlays Spending on assets that last more than one year, such as buildings, roads and equipment. (05) Infrastructure only. Capital outlays also include equipment Capitalization threshold The unit cost from which an item is recorded as property, plant and equipment: PHP 50,000 since 2022. The Manual of 2015 says PHP 15,000. (13) The limit for one payment from petty cash, which is another rule Carrier In the register of interfaces: the means by which a flow passes from one body or system to another, for example paper, entry by the sender, or system to system. (16) The kind of the flow, which says what passes: data, a document, an authority or money Cash advance Money given to a named officer before the expense is made. The officer must later account for it. The Manual names four kinds: for payroll, for operating expenses of a field office, for travel, and for a special purpose. (07) An advance payment to a contractor under a contract Cash budgeting The rule that an appropriation may be obligated and paid only within its fiscal year, with a short extended payment period. In force since 2019. (05) Accounting on the cash basis. The books of agencies use the accrual basis Cash program The plan of cash receipts and payments of the government by month. (11) The Notice of Cash Allocation, which is the limit for one agency that follows from the plan Certificate of availability of funds The statement of the chief accountant, before a contract is entered into, that funds are available for it. A contract without it is void. (05, 07) Box B of the obligation request, where the budget unit certifies the allotment, and Box C of the voucher, where the accountant certifies cash Claim In this atlas: the event by which the government owes an amount to a named party. A purchase that was delivered and accepted is one form. A salary for service rendered, a transfer and debt service are other forms. (07) An obligation, which is the commitment in the registry, and a voucher, which is the document that approves the claim for payment Classification A system of codes that puts amounts into classes. UACS is a classification. A classification code does not identify one transaction. (17) An identifier Commitment In BTMS, an amount reserved against an allotment before the obligation is recorded. (16) An obligation. In BTMS the commitment comes first Common fund The rule that a regular NCA may pay obligations of the current year and unpaid obligations of earlier years. (05) The General Fund Competitive bidding The general mode of procurement, open to all eligible bidders. (06) Consolidation Adding the statements of several entities into one statement, after the balances and transactions between them are removed. (08) Reconciliation, which compares two records of the same thing Constructive receipt A receipt that is recorded although no cash moves. (08, 10) A deposit of cash Contingent liability A promise of the government to pay if a stated event occurs, for example a guarantee of a loan. (07) An expense in the books, which is recorded at acceptance, and a release of allotment by DBM Due and demandable A claim is due and demandable when the goods, services or works were delivered, rendered or completed, and accepted. (17) A classification code Indicator A measure with a unit, for which a target is set for the year. (18) Inspection and acceptance Two acts by two officers. (18) Evaluation and audit Monthly Disbursement Program The plan of payments of an agency by month. It is the basis of the NCA. (14) The Notice of Transfer of Allocation, which other documents shorten to the same three letters Net lending The amount that the national government lends to government corporations, less repayments. t: Reference F. Sources and verification
x: Part of the Philippine PFM Atlas. Facts on current events as of 8 October 2026. The sources of section 2.6, the Government Auditing Code and the Implementing Rules of the procurement law were read as files from 10 to 12 October 2026. The issuances of the GPPB of section 2.7 were read through the web tool on 12 October 2026.

t: 1. How to read the "Basis" marks in this atlas
x: Every table of steps in this atlas has a column named "Basis". Every diagram file contains comment lines that name its sources. The marks have these meanings. Mark Meaning A code in square brackets, for example [NBC599] I opened this source during this work and found the fact in it. The code is explained in section 2. A section number after the code, for example [RA12009 s.49] , gives the place in the source. GK General knowledge. I wrote this from what I know about Philippine PFM, and I did not open a source for it during this work. It is probably correct in substance, but a number, a name or a deadline may be outdated. Check these lines first. Inference My own conclusion from two or more sources. No source states it in these words. Four limits apply to these marks. First, I read most web sources through a tool that returns a summary of the page, not the full text, so a detail may be missing or shortened. Second, some official PDF files are scanned images, and parts of them were unreadable. These cases are named in section 3. Third, rules that are set each year (release guidelines, general provisions of the budget law, the Budget Call) are given for fiscal year 2026 or 2027 and change in later years. Fourth, a quotation from a web source is a quotation that the tool returned. Where the tool gave only a summary, the atlas uses no quotation marks. Five sources were read in another way: as files, in their full text. They are the three volumes of the Government Accounting Manual [GAM-V1] [GAM-V2] [GAM-V3] , the Government Auditing Code [PD1445] and the Implementing Rules of the procurement law [IRR12009] . I converted each file to text and read the text itself, not a summary. For these five sources a program compares every quotation in the atlas with the text (section 6). A section or appendix number after the code gives the place, for example [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] for chapter 6, section 12 of Volume I, and [GAM-V2 App.32] for Appendix 32 of Volume II. Two more marks are used. "A difference between two sources" or "a difference inside the Manual" means: two texts that I read say different things, and the atlas states both and does not decide between them. Reference G, section 1 , lists these cases. "Not stated" in the register of interfaces means that the sources that I read are silent. It never means that the thing does not exist.

t: 6. The checks of quotations and of cited places
x: Two programs compare the atlas with the five sources that I hold as text. Both are in the folder tools/ of the repository. Quotations. The program tools/check_quotes.py reads every Markdown source file and every comment line of a diagram file. On each line that names one of the five sources that I hold as text (GAM-V1, GAM-V2, GAM-V3, IRR12009, PD1445) it takes each passage between quotation marks of 12 characters or more and searches it in the text files. Before the comparison it replaces line breaks by spaces and joins a word that is divided at the end of a line. A passage with three dots is divided at the dots, and each part is searched. Result of the last run, on 12 October 2026: 127 passages were found word for word. None was found only by a looser comparison, and none was missing. 11 more passages are on the list of passages that I compared myself, without the program ( tools/quotes_by_hand.txt ). 2 of them are from a form that is printed in two columns, Appendix 11 of Volume II. 1 is the title in the properties of the file of the Implementing Rules. 8 are quotations from other sources that stand on a line that also names one of the five sources. Cited places. The program tools/check_refs.py takes every citation of one of the five sources, in square brackets or in a table cell, and tests that the cited place exists in the text: the chapter and section of Volume I, the annex, the appendix of Volume II, the section of the Rules, the section of the Code. Result of the last run, on 12 October 2026: 2,632 citations of a place were tested, and every place exists. The program counts a place each time that a line cites it. Numbers. On 12 October 2026 a third program compared the numbers of each line that cites a section of the five sources with the numbers in the text of the cited sections: amounts, percentages, periods, account codes. It cannot decide anything alone, because a line also contains row numbers and numbers from other sources. It listed the numbers that it did not find, and I examined each one. Five were real: in each case the number was correct, and the citation named another section than the one that contains the number. I corrected these five citations (one basis in chapter 07 on disallowances, three bases of steps of diagram 07i , one comment line of diagram 15d ). All other numbers on the list were row numbers, or numbers from a source that is not among the five. This program is not in the repository, because its list needs a reader. What the checks do not show. They do not show that a statement without quotation marks and without a number is correct: a cited section can exist and say something else than the atlas says. They do not cover sources that I read through the web tool. The text files are my conversions of the five documents, and the repository does not contain them, so a reader who wants to repeat the checks must convert the same documents to text. The second program names the files that it expects. Beside these programs, I compared the statements of the text with my notes from the sources while I wrote, and for a number of statements I opened the source text again. This is a check by the same reader who wrote the text. It is weaker than a check by a second person.

t: Philippine PFM Atlas
x: A set of diagrams and descriptions that map public financial management (PFM) of the Philippine national government: the process, the authorities that participate in it, and their information systems. Facts on current events are as of 8 October 2026. The atlas is based mainly on five texts that were read in full as files: the three volumes of the Government Accounting Manual, the Government Auditing Code, and the Implementing Rules of the procurement law. Book VI of the Administrative Code, the release rules of the budget, the issuances of the GPPB after the Implementing Rules and many other sources were read through a tool that returns a summary with short quotations. Reference F lists every source and the way it was read, and in section 5 the decisions that shape the atlas. This atlas is not an official publication of the Philippine government. It does not replace the laws, circulars and manuals that it cites.

t: 1. Where to start
x: Read 00_BIG_PICTURE.md . It gives the whole on a few pages and contains the eight overview diagrams. Open the chapter of the part you need (section 4 below). Each chapter explains one process and contains its diagrams. Use the reference files for the authorities, the information systems, the documents, the laws, the terms, the sources, and the open questions (section 5). Before a diagram is reused for another purpose, read section 5.1 of the big picture. It names the nine kinds of arrows of this atlas and, for each kind, an observation that would show an arrow to be wrong. To see what is not settled, read Reference G : 18 differences between sources and 68 facts that I could not verify, each with a number.

t: 6. How accuracy is marked
x: Every table of steps has a column "Basis". Every diagram file contains comment lines that name its sources. Mark Meaning A code in square brackets, for example [NBC599] or [RA12009 s.49] I opened this source during this work and found the fact in it. Reference F explains each code GK General knowledge. I wrote the line from what I know, and I did not open a source for it. Check these lines first Inference My own conclusion from two or more sources. No source states it in these words Two more marks are used. Where two texts that I read say different things, the text says "a difference between two sources", states both, and does not decide. In the register of interfaces, "Not stated" means that the sources are silent. It does not mean that a flow or a system is absent. How the sources were read. Five sources were read as files, word for word: the three volumes of the Government Accounting Manual of 2015, the Government Auditing Code of 1978, and the Implementing Rules of the procurement law as approved in February 2025. A program compares every quotation from these five with the text (section 10). I read the other sources through a tool that returns a summary of the page with short quotations, not the full text. Some official files are scanned images, and parts of them were unreadable. Four limits remain. The Manual is of 2015, and I checked only one later change of it, the threshold of PHP 50,000 for property. The file of the Implementing Rules is the text of February 2025. I read the list of the resolutions of the GPPB to 14 August 2026 and fourteen of them, but only as summaries. Book VI of the Administrative Code was read as summaries with quotations, and its chapter 2 was not opened. Two facts of 2026 are known to me only from press releases and press reports: Executive Order No. 126 on the COMPASS portal, and the state of the FY 2027 budget bill. Rules that are set each year are given for fiscal year 2026 or 2027.

t: 7. Conventions in the diagram files
x: Header comments. Each .mmd file has comment lines near its start (they begin with %% ). Each .puml file has comment lines that begin with ' . The lines have fixed openings: Opening of the line Content QUESTION THIS DIAGRAM ANSWERS: The one question that the diagram answers IDEA: The idea in plain words READING: How to read the shapes, arrows and colours SOURCES: The sources, by code GENERAL KNOWLEDGE, NOT OPENED IN A SOURCE HERE: The parts of the diagram that are not from an opened source INFERENCE: A statement in the diagram that is my own conclusion MORE SOURCES: Sources for parts of the diagram that the line SOURCES: does not name Other openings, for example NOT STATED IN THE SOURCES I READ: Limits of the diagram Colours. In the overview diagrams and in most others, the colour of a frame or box marks the kind of authority: blue for the executive (DBM, DEPDev, the President and the collegial bodies), purple for Congress, green for spending agencies and local governments, yellow for the finance side (DOF and its bureaus, the Treasury accounts, the banks), light orange for COA and the other independent bodies, a stronger orange for BTMS, and grey for parties outside government and for planned items. Some diagrams use colour for another purpose, and their READING: line says so. Arrows. In diagrams that show exchanges: a thin solid arrow is a decision or a document, a thick arrow is money, a dotted arrow is information. In the two component diagrams of chapter 16 , a solid black arrow means that a source describes an electronic channel, and a dashed grey arrow means paper, an entry by staff in a record of their own body, or a carrier that the sources do not state. The label of each arrow says which. In diagram 17b the colour of an arrow says whether a field of a form holds the number that links two records. Section 5.1 of the big picture lists all kinds of arrows. Numbers in sequence diagrams. The steps are numbered by Mermaid. The tables of steps in the chapters use the same numbers. One technical mark in sequence diagrams. A step that an actor performs alone (a message from an actor to itself) ends with a line that contains only #nbsp; . This code means a non-breaking space, which is a space character that the program does not delete. The empty line moves the text away from the step number in the picture. It has no other meaning. Why some diagrams are in PlantUML. Mermaid is the main notation. Eight diagrams are in PlantUML because Mermaid cannot draw them well: six lane diagrams with parallel bars or decision points (00f, 03b, 06d, 07b, 14d, 19b), and two component diagrams that place systems inside frames of their owner institutions (16b, 16g).

t: 8. How to render the diagrams
x: The images in rendered/ were made with Mermaid 11.16 (through the command-line tool mmdc , version 11.16.0) and PlantUML 1.2026.8. Afterwards each image was reduced to 256 colours, which makes the files smaller and does not change what is shown. In the repository the script tools/render_diagrams.py draws the images from the code files in src/diagrams/ and reduces their colours. Its first lines say which programs it needs. One diagram can also be drawn by hand: The code can also be pasted into an online editor for Mermaid or PlantUML. Most .mmd files start with a block between two lines of three hyphens. This block sets the title and one layout option, and it needs a recent version of Mermaid.

t: 9. Notes on the Markdown files
x: In the chapters, each Mermaid diagram appears as a code block that many Markdown viewers draw as a picture. The code block is the content of the .mmd file without its comment lines. The comment lines are shown above the block as a list. Each PlantUML diagram appears as an image from rendered/ , with its code below it. The tables of steps were generated from the sequence diagrams, so the numbers and texts of the steps agree with the diagrams. Each paragraph is one line of text, without line breaks inside it. In the big picture, four blocks stand between a line <!-- site:NAME --> and a line <!-- /site:NAME --> : the five parts, the four lines, the meeting points and the two cases. Markdown viewers do not show these lines. The website of the atlas shows the four blocks on its home page as well. The folder reference/ also contains three files in CSV form (text with commas between the values, which a spreadsheet or a program can open). diagram_index.csv has one row for each diagram: its ID, its form, its title, the question it answers, its files, and the Markdown files that contain it. steps_register.csv has one row for each numbered step of the 20 sequence diagrams that have a table of steps: who acts, towards whom, what is done, and the basis. interface_register.csv is the register of Reference B, section 4 , with the columns number, side, from, to, what passes, kind, carrier, stage of use, check of both sides, and basis. The three files are written by the same script that builds the Markdown files, so they agree with them. The Markdown files of the atlas are generated. A change is made in the source file in src/ , and the script tools/build_atlas.py writes the file again. A change made only in docs/atlas/ is lost at the next build.

t: 10. How to check the atlas
x: The folder tools/ of the repository contains the scripts. They need Python 3. Run them from the root of the repository. The first script tests that the parts of the atlas agree with each other. It checks Why Every diagram file has an image, states its question and names its sources A diagram without a stated question cannot be judged No Mermaid flowchart uses a reserved word of Mermaid, for example end , class or call , as the name of a node Such a file looks correct as text and cannot be drawn Every code block in a Markdown file is equal to a diagram file, and every diagram file is in a Markdown file A description and its diagram must not differ Every link leads to a file that exists Every source code in square brackets and in a column "Basis" is defined in Reference F A code without a definition cannot be traced Every table row has the right number of cells, and no cell of a column "Basis" is empty The CSV files agree with the diagram files and with Reference B . The steps in the register agree with the sequence diagrams. Each row of the register of interfaces uses only the allowed values for kind, carrier and stage of use Every paragraph is on one line No file contains a placeholder that was not filled With the option --render the script also draws every Mermaid file, if the program mmdc is installed. The second script compares quotations with the source texts. It reads every line that names one of the five sources that I hold as text, takes each passage between quotation marks of 12 characters or more, and searches it in the text files. The repository does not contain these text files, because they are conversions of the five documents. A reader who wants to repeat the check must convert the same five documents to plain text and put them in one folder. The file tools/quotes_by_hand.txt lists the passages that the script cannot find for a stated reason and that I compared myself. The third script tests that every place that the atlas cites in the same five sources exists: that Volume I of the Manual has a chapter 6 with a section 63, that the Rules have a section 71.2.8, that Volume II has an Appendix 32. It needs the same folder of source texts. The script tools/verify_counts.py runs the second and the third script and tests that their results agree with the numbers written in Reference F, section 6 . No script tests whether a statement without quotation marks is true. The third script shows that a cited section exists, and not that the section says what the atlas says. That needs a reader with the sources. At the last run the first script reported no problem, and all 85 diagrams were drawn with the versions named in section 8. The results of the second and of the third script are in Reference F, section 6 . When the second or the third script is run on the built files in docs/atlas/ and not on src/ , its numbers are higher, because each chapter repeats the comment lines of its diagrams.

t: 11. What the atlas does not cover
x: Tax policy and tax administration beyond the flow of collections and refunds. Social security institutions and government financial institutions. The Bangsamoro region and its block grant. The bodies with fiscal autonomy. The accounting standards for single subjects, for example financial instruments and leases: the Manual has a chapter for each, and I did not read these chapters. Amounts of guarantees and of other contingent liabilities. What agencies do in practice where practice differs from the rules: the atlas draws the rules and reports what one assessment of 2025 says about practice. Reference G, section 3 , gives the state of coverage for every subject, with its least certain part.

t: Diagram 00a: The whole of PFM for the national government: what happens in order, what happens at the same time, and the chapter for each part
x: Question: which parts form public financial management (PFM) in the Philippines, which of them follow one another, which of them happen at the same time, and which chapter of this atlas describes each one? Question: which parts form public financial management (PFM) in the Philippines, which of them follow one another, which of them happen at the same time, and which chapter of this atlas describes each one? Idea: only the decisions of part A follow one another for one fiscal year. In part B three lines of steps run at the same time, and money may leave the Treasury only where all three have a result for the same amount ( diagram 00d ). Part C is not a later step: every act of part B writes a record at the time of the act. Part D happens at the end of each month, quarter and year. Part E is what stays after the year. How to read it: a solid arrow between two frames = the lower frame needs the result of the upper frame. The dotted arrow from B to C = every act in B writes a record in C at the same time. Inside a frame, an arrow = the order of the steps of that line. The frames at the sides are active during the whole year. The cycle is not a simple loop: results return to the plans and budgets of LATER fiscal years, so the last node is drawn as an exit and not as an arrow back to part A. Why the records stand at every act: the Manual records the allotment and the obligation in registries when they occur, makes the first journal entry when the Notice of Cash Allocation arrives, and records the payable when the delivery is accepted, before any payment [GAM-V1 Annex H] . Recording is therefore not a step after payment. Sources: DBM primer on the budget process [PRIMER] , FY 2027 Budget Call [NBM156] , FY 2026 release guidelines [NBC599] , procurement law [RA12009] , reporting circular [JC2019-1] , the Government Accounting Manual for the records of each unit and the order of the entries [GAM-V1 Ch.2 s.8, s.12, Ch.3, Annex H] , Auditing Code [PD1445 s.41] , PFM Reforms Roadmap 2024-2028 [ROADMAP2024] . The arrangement in five parts is my own. Limit: local governments and government corporations have their own complete cycles ( chapters 14 and 15). Here they appear only where national money passes to them.

t: Diagram 00d: Three lines of steps, the three points where they must meet, and the record that each act writes (one payment under a contract)
x: Question: which conditions must all be true before one payment to a contractor can be made, who makes each condition true, and which record is written at each act? Question: which conditions must all be true before one payment to a contractor can be made, who makes each condition true, and which record is written at each act? Idea: a payment is not the end of one line of steps. Three lines of steps run at the same time: legal authority, the claim, and cash. A payment is possible only when they meet. The fourth line, the records, does not come after the payment: each act writes its record when it happens. A diagram with one line of steps hides both facts. Form (Petri-net style): rounded node p = a state that can be true or not yet true. Rectangle t = an act by the persons named in it. An act with two incoming solid arrows needs BOTH states. A grey node r = a record. A dotted arrow from an act to a grey node = the act writes this record at the time of the act. Colours: blue = legal authority to spend. Green = the claim: the contract, the work and its acceptance. Orange = cash. Grey = records, reports and audit. The small separate chain (pT to p19): the closing of a period does not follow one payment. It follows the calendar, and it uses all records that exist on that day. The audit of one paid transaction (t14) follows the payment, because the paid voucher goes to the auditor with the daily report of payment orders issued [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.56] . The three meeting points: t3 (allotment meets award), t6 (obligation meets accepted delivery), t6c (the claim meets cash authority). The third point is the certificate "cash available" on the voucher: the head of accounting looks into the registry of the NCA, and when the balance is not sufficient the voucher is kept until cash is available [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] . No check and no payment order may be issued without a covering NCA [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.3] . THE EXCEPTION AT t6: the law allows no advance payment without the prior approval of the President, and no payment without a certificate that the delivery was inspected and accepted [PD1445 s.88] . The procurement rules give that approval in defined cases: for works, an advance of not more than 15 percent on the written request of the contractor and against an irrevocable standby letter of credit, a bank guarantee or a surety bond [IRR12009 s.71.2.5] . In that case the security (p8b) replaces the accepted delivery (p8). The dashed green path shows it. Diagram 07i follows such a contract with amounts. The dotted arrow into t9 is a read arc: DBM consults the cash position of the Treasury but does not consume it when it issues an NCA. Limits of this form: (1) allotment and NCA are balances, so each token would need an amount. t: Diagram 00f: One fiscal year from plan to audit: who acts at each step, and which record is written there (national government agency)
x: Question: for one fiscal year, which authority acts at each step from plan to audit, where do two lines of work run at the same time and then have to meet, and at which step is each record written? Question: for one fiscal year, which authority acts at each step from plan to audit, where do two lines of work run at the same time and then have to meet, and at which step is each record written? Idea: the steps of deciding (plan, fiscal frame, proposal, law) follow one another. In execution, two lines of work run at the same time three times, and each time both must be finished before the next step. The records are not a last step: the text of each step names the record that is written at that step. Only the closing of a period and the audit of the statements follow the calendar. How to read it: one column (lane) = one authority. Read from top to bottom. A thick horizontal bar that splits the flow = the branches run in parallel. The bar that closes them = BOTH branches must be finished before the next step. A line that starts with "Record:" names what is written at that step, and by which unit. Why PlantUML: Mermaid has no activity diagram with lanes and parallel bars. Why the records stand at every act: the Manual shows that the registries are written at the allotment and at the obligation, the first journal entry at the receipt of the NCA, and the payable at the accepted delivery [GAM-V1 Annex H] . The certificate "cash available" on the voucher is a separate step, because it is the point where the claim meets the cash authority [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] . Sources: [PRIMER] [NBM156] [CONST] [NBC599] [RA12009] [PD1445 s.41, s.86] [GAM-V1 Ch.3, Ch.6 s.12, s.56, Ch.19 s.60, Ch.21, Annex H] [GAM-V2 App.32] [CL2013-16A] [JC2019-1] [COA2011-002] . Steps marked (GK) are general knowledge, not opened in a source during this work.

t: Diagram 00h: One contract with dates: a school building paid from the FY 2026 budget (invented example, real rules)
x: Question: the other diagrams show the order of steps. How long does each step take for one contract, in which fiscal year does each step occur, and on which date is each record written? Question: the other diagrams show the order of steps. How long does each step take for one contract, in which fiscal year does each step occur, and on which date is each record written? Idea: one contract extends over three calendar years. Its budget is prepared in the year before, the work is done in the budget year, and the last progress payment, the release of the retention money and the audit occur in the year after. The four sections are the four lines of steps of diagram 00d : authority, the claim, cash, records. The records are written on the dates of the acts, and not after the last payment. THE EXAMPLE IS INVENTED. The agency, the amounts and the dates of the single steps are not real. The rules that fix the earliest and latest dates are real, and they are listed here with their sources. The example: an agency builds a school building for PHP 48 million. The amount is a capital outlay in the FY 2026 budget law, without a pre-condition for release. The contractor asks for an advance of 15 percent. The work takes nine months and is billed in three parts. Rules used, with sources: the agency may hold the bidding before the budget law exists, once the President's budget is submitted, but it may not award before the funding is in effect and the head of the agency has approved the final procurement plan [IRR12009 s.12] [RA12009 s.12] . The FY 2026 budget law took effect on 5 January 2026, and the law itself is the allotment for items without pre-conditions [NBC599] . Award within 60 days from the opening of bids, contract within 10 days after the notice of award [IRR12009 s.66, s.67] , notice to proceed within 3 days [RA12009 s.66] . The chief accountant certifies that funds are available before the contract [PD1445 s.86] . Advance to a works contractor: not more than 15 percent, on written request and against a letter of credit, bank guarantee or surety bond [IRR12009 s.71.2.5] . Progress billing not more often than once a month. Each bill is reduced by the part of the advance that is recovered and by the retention money [IRR12009 s.71.2.7, s.71.2.8] . Defects liability period of one year from completion to final acceptance. The retention money is due for release upon final acceptance [IRR12009 s.90.2.2, s.71.2.8] . A regular NCA lapses at the end of its quarter, and the regular NCA of a later period also covers payables of earlier years [NBC599 s.4.2] . The bank credits the payee within two banking days after it receives the payment order [CL2018-14] . Quarterly reports within 30 days after each quarter, and the report on unpaid obligations within 30 days after the year [JC2019-1] . Year-end statements to COA by 14 February, annual report of COA by 30 September [PD1445 s.41] . Capital outlays of FY 2026 may be obligated until 31 December 2027 (the table in my copy was partly unreadable) [NBC599 s.3.3] . Records, with sources: the obligation is entered in the registry and has no journal entry. An advance is recorded as Advances to Contractors. Each certified progress billing is recorded as Construction in Progress and as Accounts Payable. At the turn-over of the completed building the cost moves to the account Buildings. Retention money is held as Guaranty/Security Deposits Payable until it is released [GAM-V1 Ch.3 s.15, Ch.10 s.8, Annex H] . Where the example fails on purpose: the third bill is certified on 20 November 2026, but the cash authority of the fourth quarter is fully used. The contractor is paid on 15 February 2027. During these weeks the amount is a cost of construction and a payable in the books, an obligation in the registry, and no disbursement. Diagram 08c explains these measures. General knowledge, not opened in a source here: the dates of the budget preparation in 2025 (the pattern of 2026 is used), and the month in which the audit report of the agency is issued.

Short labels: "change within the limit" = an amendment to order (goods) or a variation order (works) of not more than 10 percent of the original contract price, or up to 20 percent with the approval of the head of the procuring entity. t: Diagram 06f: A contract that lasts more than one year: the Multi-Year Contractual Authority (MYCA)

Question: an appropriation is valid for one year, but a bridge takes three years to build. What allows an agency to sign one contract for the whole work, and where does the money of each year come from? Idea: two different permissions are needed. The MYCA allows the agency to SIGN a contract for more than one year. The budget law of each year provides the MONEY of that year. The first does not replace the second. How to read it: top = which authorization is needed, by source of money. Middle = from the MYCA to the contract. Bottom frame = what is repeated in every year of the contract. Sources: the MYCA is defined as the authority to procure multi-year projects in the form and under the conditions set by DBM [IRR12009 s.5] . It is required before any procurement activity for locally funded multi-year contracts, DBM issues it, and its total project cost is the basis of the Approved Budget for the Contract. The cases by source of money: sections 9.1.1 to 9.1.4 [IRR12009 s.9] . Request documents, no change after issue, yearly amounts in the Tier 1 proposal, the note on the form about yearly obligations, and the rule that regular and recurring services no longer need a MYCA [CL2025-6] . DBM issues the MYCA under the cash budgeting order [EO91] . Renewal of contracts for regular and recurring services when funds are available [IRR12009 s.18] . From a press report of a DBM statement [GMA-MYCA] : the example of a bridge of PHP 10 billion programmed at 3, 4 and 3 billion in three years, and the statement that projects financed by foreign loans do not need a MYCA before the contract is signed. Inference: the grey box at the bottom. No source that I read says what the agency does when the budget law of a year contains less than the amount planned for that year.

t: Diagram 07a: From obligation to payment: who certifies what, and which record each step writes (goods bought by a national agency, paid by payment order)

What the diagram shows: every certification before step 20 is made by an officer of the agency itself. The first outside check is by the servicing bank (step 20). The bank checks the payment order and the cash limit. It does not check the delivery. COA examines after payment. The records are written during the process: the obligation at step 2, the payable at steps 7 and 8, the use of the cash authority at step 11, the payment at steps 27 and 28. Tax withheld [GAM-V1 Ch.6 ss.60-62] . The wording of the certificates is that of the forms [GAM-V2 App.11, App.32, App.42, App.61, App.62] . Certificate of funds before a contract [PD1445 s.86] . Copy of the summary list to BTr and replenishment [CL2013-16A] . Electronic facility of the bank [eMDS] . Two banking days [CL2018-14] . Audit after payment [COA2011-002] . The text of the procedure calls the certificate of the accountant Box B and the approval Box C [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] . The diagram follows the form. The diagram follows the worked example. (3) The Manual lets the cashier certify the summary list [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.56] . The circular of 2013 names the head of accounting [CL2013-16A] . t: Diagram 07b: The three meeting points before a payment, and the record written at each step (national agency, contract for goods)

Question: which lines of work must BOTH be finished before the next step of a payment may happen, and which record does each unit write at its step? Idea: a payment needs three meetings. (1) An allotment and an award must both exist before the contract is signed and the obligation is recorded. (2) The obligation and an accepted delivery must both exist before the amount is a payable. (3) The claim in order and a cash authority (NCA) must both exist before the head of accounting certifies "cash available" on the voucher. The payment order follows the third meeting. The Mermaid diagram 00d shows the same structure as a net without lanes. Where the meeting points are: the Manual places the check of the NCA at Box C of the voucher [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] , and its worked example records the payable at the accepted delivery [GAM-V1 Annex H] . Sources: [NBC599] allotment and NCA. [RA12009 s.12] no award before funding. [PD1445 s.86] certificate of funds before a contract. [GAM-V1 Ch.3 s.15] obligation. [GAM-V1 Ch.8 s.15] delivery, inspection, acceptance. [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12, s.56] voucher, registry of the NCA, payment order, daily report. [GAM-V2 App.11, App.32, App.42, App.62] wording of the forms. [GAM-V1 Annex H] entries of the agency and of the Treasury. [CL2013-16A] copy to BTr and replenishment. [COA2011-002] audit after payment. General knowledge (GK), not opened in a source here: what the bank checks before it debits the sub-account.

t: Diagram 07c: The chain of certifications for one payment: who signs, what the signature states, and who checks it

Question: a payment depends on several signatures. What exactly does each signature assert, and is that assertion checked by anyone outside the agency before the money leaves? How to read it: each row is one document. Left = who signs. Right = what the signature states, in the words of the form where the text is in quotation marks. The colour of the row shows who makes the statement: green = an officer of the agency, yellow = the bank, orange = the auditor. What the diagram shows: the facts "the goods were delivered" and "the delivery meets the order" are stated only by officers of the agency, and by two different officers. t: Diagram 07d: Payment and settlement: how money moves from the Treasury Single Account to the payee (Modified Disbursement System)

Question: the agency holds no cash for its regular budget. Through which accounts does the money pass when the agency pays, at which moment does cash leave the Treasury, and on which date does each party record the payment? Idea: under the Modified Disbursement System (MDS) the servicing bank pays first, from a fund that the Treasury keeps filled. The NCA is only a limit recorded at the bank. The Manual says of the account Cash-MDS in the books of the agency that "there is no actual cash with the GSBs" [GAM-V1 Ch.19 s.56] . Cash leaves the Treasury Single Account when BTr replenishes the bank for payments already made. Three dates for one payment: the agency credits its account Cash-MDS on the day of the daily report of payment orders issued. That report also contains payment orders that are not yet delivered to the bank [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.52, s.54] . The bank credits the payee 24 to 48 hours after it receives the payment order [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.2] . The Treasury records the subsidy to the agency when the bank has paid [GAM-V1 Annex H] . The monthly bank reconciliation explains the differences [GAM-V1 Ch.21] . Sources: NCA credited to MDS sub-accounts at LBP, DBP and PVB, lapsing at the end of the quarter [NBC599] . Receipt of the NCA in the books, no official receipt [GAM-V1 Ch.5 s.38] . Payment order, summary list, copies, same-day copy to BTr for the replenishment of the MDS Seed Fund, validated copy, invalidated items [GAM-V1 Ch.6 ss.50-56] [CL2013-16A] . Daily replenishment of servicing banks [PRIMER] . Electronic facility of LBP, adopted by a joint order of DBM and DOF of 12 March 2015 [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.58] [eMDS] . Checks, the daily advice of checks issued and cancelled, stale checks [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.2, s.12, s.44] . Bank reconciliation [GAM-V1 Ch.21] [PD1445 s.74] . Entry for the unused NCA [GAM-V1 Ch.19 s.55] . Treasury Single Account as a unified structure of government bank accounts [BTR-SITE] . Daily bank reconciliation in BTMS, payments by PESONet and InstaPay [BTMS-SITE] [CL2025-8] . General knowledge, not opened in a source here: steps 9 and 10 (the instruction to BSP and the entries at BSP).

t: Diagram 07f: States of one cash advance, from grant to liquidation
x: Question: a cash advance leaves the Treasury before any delivery is accepted. How does the government ensure that the money is later accounted for? Question: a cash advance leaves the Treasury before any delivery is accepted. How does the government ensure that the money is later accounted for? Idea: a cash advance is money given to a named officer, who is personally accountable for it until he or she presents proof of how it was spent (liquidation) and returns the rest. In the books the money is a receivable from the officer until then, and not an expense. Sources: the three rules of the law: only for a legally authorized specific purpose, to be liquidated as soon as the purpose is served, and no new advance before the earlier one is settled [PD1445 s.89] . Bond, permanent appointment of disbursing officers, no transfer between officers [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.14] . Time limits: an advance for payroll within 5 days after the end of the pay period, local travel within 30 days after return, foreign travel within 60 days [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.15, ss.25-29] . Petty cash: replenished when 75 percent is used, never closed at the end of the year [GAM-V1 Ch.6 ss.35-39] . The accounts: Advances for Payroll, Advances to Officers and Employees, Advances for Operating Expenses, Advances to Special Disbursing Officer [GAM-V1 Ch.5 s.38, Ch.6 s.19] . A disallowance enters the books only when it is final and executory, as a receivable [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.46] . Bonding is administered by BTr [EO449] . Weakness reported: a part of the advances, in particular advances to government corporations, was not liquidated at the end of 2023 (indicator 27.3, score C) [PEFA2025] . General knowledge, not opened in a source here: the demand letter and the withholding of salary. They are in COA Circular No. 97-002, which the Manual names and which I did not open.

t: Diagram 07g: When a step fails: who acts, where the transaction continues, and which record shows it
x: Question: diagrams 07a and 07b show the path when every check succeeds. What happens when one check fails, and where can a reader of the records see that it failed? Question: diagrams 07a and 07b show the path when every check succeeds. What happens when one check fails, and where can a reader of the records see that it failed? How to read it: each row is one kind of failure, in the order of the process. The rows are separate cases, not a sequence. Column 1 = what fails. Column 2 = who acts and how. Column 3 = where the transaction continues. Column 4 (grey) = the record or report in which the failure is visible. Why it matters for a process model: each row is a path that leaves the main sequence. A model that contains only the main sequence cannot represent unpaid obligations, lapsed authority or recovered payments. Sources: row 1, the registry balance is taken at every entry to prevent obligations above the allotment [GAM-V1 Ch.3 s.10] ; changes of allotment and their approval [NBC599 s.3.13] ; BTMS refuses an obligation above the allotment [CL2025-8] . Row 2, items that do not conform are returned to the supplier [GAM-V1 Ch.8 s.15] ; damages of one tenth of one percent of the cost of the delayed goods for every day of delay, and the right to rescind when they reach 10 percent of the contract price [IRR12009 s.71.1.4] ; take-over of an ended contract by negotiated procurement [IRR12009 s.35.3] ; notice of adjustment of an obligation [GAM-V1 Ch.3 ss.13-14] . Row 3, check of completeness and of the index of payments [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] . Row 4, the voucher is kept when the registry of the NCA shows no balance [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.12] ; a regular NCA lapses at the end of the quarter, additional NCAs, and the regular NCA covers payables of the current and of earlier years [NBC599 s.4.2] ; aging of unpaid obligations in FAR 3 and monthly disbursements in FAR 4 [JC2019-1] . Row 5, a payment order may be invalidated when the bank branch, the account name or the account number does not agree with the bank records; journal entry and new payment order [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.54] ; remarks of the bank [CL2018-14] . Row 6, stale checks and the entry that restores the payable [GAM-V1 Ch.6 ss.44-45] ; the law gives two years [PD1445 s.97] . Row 7, unused balances revert to the unappropriated surplus of the General Fund [NBC599 s.3.6] [EO292-B6 s.28] . Row 8, transfers are not disbursements until the receiver has used them for accepted deliveries [NBC599 s.3.4] ; reports of the receiver within ten days after each month and return of the unused balance [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.63] ; report FAR 1-C [JC2019-1] . Row 9, notices of suspension and of disallowance, appeal, finality, order of execution [COA2009-006] ; a disallowance enters the books only when it is final and executory [GAM-V1 Ch.6 s.46] . Weakness reported: the stock of expenditure arrears in 2023 was above 10 percent of expenditure (indicator 22.1, score D) [PEFA2025] .

t: Diagram 07h: Kinds of payment: what creates the claim, what proves it before payment, and what the books record at that time
x: Question: a purchase is paid after a contract and an accepted delivery. Question: a purchase is paid after a contract and an accepted delivery. What replaces these two things in the other kinds of payment, which document proves the claim before the money leaves, and what do the books show at that moment? Idea: every payment needs legal authority, cash and records in the same way ( diagram 00d ). The kinds of payment differ only in the event that makes the government owe the money, and in the document that proves this event. In rows 2 and 5 the money leaves before anything is delivered. The rules then require a security or a bond, and the books record a receivable and not an expense. How to read it: each row is one kind of payment. The rows are separate cases, not a sequence. Question: when a contractor receives an advance and is then paid by progress billings, which amounts leave the Treasury on which occasion, what is retained, and what do the books show at each step? Idea: the advance is not a cost. It is money of the government in the hands of the contractor, covered by a security, and it is recovered from the later billings. A part of each payment is kept as retention money until final acceptance. Over the whole contract the payments, the retention and the tax together equal the contract price. The example: the amounts and the accounts are those of the worked example of the Manual for a building of PHP 800,000 [GAM-V1 Ch.10 s.8] . The Manual is of 2015 and its example follows the rules of that time. The rules of 2025: advance of not more than 15 percent, on the written request of the contractor and against an irrevocable standby letter of credit, a bank guarantee or a surety bond [IRR12009 s.71.2.5] . Progress billing not more often than once a month, checked and certified by the engineer of the agency. Deductions: work already paid, the part of the advance that is recovered, retention money, third-party liabilities, uncorrected defects [IRR12009 s.71.2.7] . Retention of 10 percent of the amount due before any deduction, from every progress payment until 50 percent of the works are completed, and released upon final acceptance [IRR12009 s.71.2.8] . Performance security before the contract is signed: 10 percent for works in cash or bank instruments, 30 percent as surety bond [IRR12009 s.68] . Damages for delay: at least one tenth of one percent of the cost of the unperformed portion for every day [IRR12009 s.71.2.4] . Defects liability period of one year from completion [IRR12009 s.90.2.2] . Differences between the example and the rules of 2025: (1) the example retains 10 percent of the payable after the advance is recovered (34,000). The rules of 2025 base the retention on the amount due before any deduction, and stop it after 50 percent of the works when the work is satisfactory and on schedule. (2) The performance security of the example is 75,000. Ten percent of the contract price would be 80,000. (3) The example computes the damages as one tenth of one percent of the contract. The rules of 2025 use the cost of the unperformed portion. Check of the arithmetic: cash to the contractor 120,000 + 282,200 + 282,200 + 68,000 = 752,400. Tax withheld 23,800 + 23,800 = 47,600. Together 800,000, the contract price.

Question: inside one national agency, which unit keeps which record, from which document it is written, which unit passes its record to which other unit, and from which records are the reports built? Idea: four units of one agency write about the same money. The BUDGET UNIT keeps registries: lists with running balances that follow legal authority (appropriation, allotment, obligation, disbursement). The ACCOUNTING UNIT keeps the books: double entry on the accrual basis (assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses). The CASH UNIT keeps the records of receipts, checks and payment orders, and it reports to accounting every day. The PROPERTY UNIT keeps the cards of the items in stock and in use. The budget reports come from the registries. The financial statements come from the books. One statement, the comparison of budget and actual amounts, needs both. How to read it: top row (grey) = source documents. Blue frame = budget unit. Green frame = accounting unit. White frames = cash unit and property unit. Yellow = reports. A solid arrow = this document or record is the source of the next record. A dotted arrow = the two records are compared with each other. Numbers in brackets: "App." is the number of the form in Volume II of the Manual [GAM-V2] . Sources: the list of journals, ledgers and registries [GAM-V1 Ch.2 s.12] . Registries of the budget unit and the rule that a balance is extracted at every entry [GAM-V1 Ch.3 ss.5-12] . Daily reports of the cash unit [GAM-V1 Ch.5 s.39, Ch.6 s.52, s.56] . Documents that are posted to the journals [GAM-V1 Ch.19 s.59] . Ledger cards of accounting and cards of the property unit, and their reconciliation [GAM-V1 Ch.8 s.9, Ch.10 s.42] . The six statements [GAM-V1 Ch.2 s.11] .
